articleTitle: Software Size Measurement Using Data Complexities (Case Study: Marketing Kit Monitoring System)
publicationTitle: 2024 11th International Conference on Electrical Engineering, Computer Science and Informatics (EECSI)
abstract: Software size estimation calculations often do not consider data complexity. However, in practice, data is considered an integral part of the system, so it needs to be taken into account in software size estimation. The combination of Common Software Measurement International Consortium (COSMIC) Functional Size Measurement and Database Complexity Index (DBCI) is the main method in estimating the size of marketing tool monitoring system. This research involves 4 stages, which include: (1) actual business calculation, (2) database complexity calculation using DBCI, (3) data movement complexity calculation using COSMIC FSM, and (4) marketing tool monitoring system size estimation. The findings of this study are that the level of data movement complexity based on COSMIC FSM is 78, while the database complexity is 236. The comparison between the results of software size estimation and actual effort is as follows 141.54 percent. A limitation of this study is the absence of source code calculations or other methods, which causes fluctuations in the comparison between estimated and actual effort.

articleTitle: Improving Software Size Estimation Using Data Complexity (Case Study: Research and Community Service Monitoring Apps)
publicationTitle: 2024 11th International Conference on Electrical Engineering, Computer Science and Informatics (EECSI)
abstract: The Research and Community Service Monitoring Apps is an essential application for managing and evaluating research and community service activities. In research related to software size estimation, the complexity of data is often disregarded. Nevertheless, in the realm of software development, data is regarded as an integral complement to the system, thus its presence is inherently factored into size computations. This study employs a hybrid approach, combining the Common Software Measurement International Consortium (COSMIC) functional size measurement with the database complexity index (DBCI). With a focus on the “Research and Community Service Monitoring Apps,” the research delineates four essential stages: (1) the calculation of actual effort, (2) determining data movement complexity through COSMIC FSM, (3) assessing database complexity using DBCI, and (4) estimating the system's size. The outcomes reveal the data movement complexity based on COSMIC FSM to be 80, while the database complexity is 196. The comparison between estimated software size and actual effort expended yields 43.75%. However, the study is limited by the absence of source code calculation or alternative methods, leading to fluctuating comparisons between estimation and actual effort.

articleTitle: Trajectory-Tracking and Centralized Control for Mapping Tasks Using Multiple Drones
publicationTitle: 2024 11th International Conference on Electrical Engineering, Computer Science and Informatics (EECSI)
abstract: This study focuses on improving multiple drones' trajectory tracking accuracy and completion time in mapping assignments. A centralized control system is applied to drones to achieve such performance. The system tracking accuracy is supported by dense square fiducial markers (SFM) as positioning media. The drone's position is assumed to be at the camera's center, leading to more precise calculations. Detecting multiple markers also ensures that the drones do not lose positional information over long distances, resulting in more accurate position estimation. The test is conducted indoors with two drones, with trajectory tracking tests performed along the x-axis and y-axis within a <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$5\times 4\ \mathrm{m}^{2}$</tex> area. The test shows that the root means squared tracking error (RMSTE) when the drones moved along the positive x-axis was 5.2 cm, less than 20% of the drone's diameter. During the mapping assignment, the drones traced an S-shaped route and obtained RMSTE values of 12.3 cm for drone A and 22.5 cm for drone B, with a travel time of 51 seconds from takeoff to landing. Therefore, detecting multiple markers improves trajectory tracking capabilities, enabling drones to perform mapping tasks efficiently, even in confined areas.

articleTitle: Prediabetes Detection Using Non-Laboratory Data with Extreme Gradient Boosting Algorithm
publicationTitle: 2024 11th International Conference on Electrical Engineering, Computer Science and Informatics (EECSI)
abstract: Diabetes Mellitus (DM), characterized by high blood glucose levels, is a dangerous condition that leads to severe long-term health issues. Meanwhile, prediabetes is a condition where individuals have an increased risk of developing type 2 DM. Early detection of prediabetes is crucial for effective DM management. Traditional detection relies on medical records and family history, but laboratory tests are not always practical. This study proposes using non-laboratory data, processed by the Extreme Gradient Boosting (XGBoost) algorithm, to identify individuals with prediabetes. The dataset used in this research includes attributes like blood pressure, weight, height, waist size, food intake, and age. Preprocessing involved removing irrelevant data and transforming numeric data into categories. The XGBoost model, applied to this dataset, achieved 0.91 for average accuracy, precision, recall, and F1-score. AUC values of the model is 0.93, demonstrating its effectiveness in distinguishing between normal and prediabetic individuals. These results suggest the potential for non-laboratory data and XGBoost in early prediabetes detection, aiding in timely intervention and improved health outcomes.

articleTitle: Power Regulation on PV and Grid With Monitoring Load Power in Residential
publicationTitle: 2024 11th International Conference on Electrical Engineering, Computer Science and Informatics (EECSI)
abstract: The need for electrical energy for residential is increasing with the increasing loads used. Apart from that, changes in the load used also affect the stability of electricity sources from photovoltaics (PV) and utility grids. Therefore, a monitoring system is needed which aims to regulate the availability of electrical energy sources and the use of loads in residential. The method used is to observe the potential of solar energy in Candisari, Semarang, Indonesia. Apart from that, he also designs logic controllers for regulating PV energy, batteries and utility grids. To build this system, 10 PV 100 Wp, 1500 Ah batteries, SCC 150 A are needed. The research results show that the electrical energy consumption used in one day is 2,796 kWh, so that in one month the average electrical energy consumption is 83.88 kWh, while PV energy production is 3,473 kWh. Load energy can be served using PV energy and batteries. Apart from that, the logic controller is able to regulate the alternation of PV and battery energy flows, while the grid energy source is only a backup and is used when the PV source or battery is disconnected.

articleTitle: Input Current Ripple Analysis of Three Phase Modified Buck-Boost Inverter
publicationTitle: 2024 11th International Conference on Electrical Engineering, Computer Science and Informatics (EECSI)
abstract: This paper proposes input current ripple analysis of three phase inverter with de-link referenced output filter, known as three phase modified buck-boost inverter. The filter consists of an inductor and two capacitors in one leg. Each phase of the inverter is independent of the remaining two phases. As a result, the inductor current ripple become similar to single phase half bridge inverter and greatly influences the input current ripple. So, exact inductor current is used in the input current ripple analysis. The formulation shows that the input current ripple is a function of modulation index, output current and load power factor. Besides that, the filter inductor also influences the input current ripple. Experiments are conducted to clarify the analytical result.

articleTitle: A Globally Convergent Improved Hybrid Method of Quasi Newton and Conjugate Gradient Method
publicationTitle: 2024 11th International Conference on Electrical Engineering, Computer Science and Informatics (EECSI)
abstract: A new algorithm which combines the Quasi-Newton (QN) method and conjugate gradient (CG) method are presented in this paper. It is denoted as <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$\mathbf{QN}-\mathbf{WAM}+$</tex> method and tested using twenty-six different standard test functions from small scale to large scale with four different initial points. All computations are conducted through Matlab software. It is then compared with the other hybrid methods based on number of iterations and CPU times and then analyzed using performance profile. From numerical results, it shows that the new algorithm with BFGS update formula as an approximation of Hessian matrix perform well and proved to be more efficient compared to other hybrid methods. Accordingly, the global convergent is theoretically prove and fulfil sufficient descent condition.

articleTitle: Introduction to GOOSE Data Communication Attack Traffic Pattern in IEC 61850
publicationTitle: 2024 11th International Conference on Electrical Engineering, Computer Science and Informatics (EECSI)
abstract: The use of lEC 61850 in electrical substation automation systems may have an impact on increasing the effectiveness and interoperability of smart grids. On the other hand, the development of connectivity will give rise to a high level of security vulnerabilities. Therefore, it is necessary to implement an effective system to protect the integrity of the infrastructure from attacks. This article will present the introduction of normal traffic patterns and attacks by means of feature extraction to improve system performance, as well as a threat detection system from an attack. Through traffic pattern analysis, the system can differentiate between attack traffic and normal traffic. This research describes what normal and attack traffic looks like on GOOSE communication data in the lEC 61850 network. The aim of this research is to identify, explain, and differentiate between normal and attack traffic which finally can increase attack detection, high response capability, and reduce false positives. In the future, it is hoped that the resulting data can reduce data complexity and traffic fluctuations in IEC 61850.

articleTitle: Design of Automatic Water Gallon Filling and Capping
publicationTitle: 2024 11th International Conference on Electrical Engineering, Computer Science and Informatics (EECSI)
abstract: Refillable drinking water depots are one of the people's choices when solving drinking water problems. Water can be drunk directly and does not need to be boiled, making it practical. There are shortcomings in refilling drinking water at nearby water depots, such as the process of filling water gallons, which is still done manually by the operator by visually observing the water level in the gallon, and the process of capping water gallons, which is also done manually by the operator. This problem can cause the filling and capping of the water gallon to be incomplete if the operator makes an error. This research aims to design a prototype of the filling and capping process at a refillable drinking water depot based on a PLC (Programmable Logic Controller) and using a robotic arm to move empty gallons onto a conveyor. Photoelectric sensors detect the presence of gallons, which automatically transfer to each process using a conveyor. The prototype created is expected to do the filling and capping refill drinking water gallons automatically. The design results show that the prototype runs well as expected, with an average time for the automatic filling and capping process of 57,40 seconds.

articleTitle: Impact of Inverter to Hybrid Power Generation: Wind Turbine and Solar Cell
publicationTitle: 2024 11th International Conference on Electrical Engineering, Computer Science and Informatics (EECSI)
abstract: In recent times, the use of Renewable Energy Sources (RES) has become a viable alternative to supply electrical energy in island regions. Ensuring energy supply security is a key factor for sustainable development in these areas. Each island region possesses unique geographical characteristics and environmental conditions. However, many island regions still rely heavily on electrical energy supplied by diesel power plants (DPP). Despite this reliance, RES has not yet been able to become the primary energy source to replace DPP. Based on these issues, the author aims to analyse the generation of solar and wind renewable energy through a hybrid power plant. This study involves research using a static wind turbine model in the form of a fan and a micro-scale Solar Power Plant (SPP). On the wind power side, the output is connected to Battery Control Unit (BCU) with Maximum Power Point Tracker (MPPT) to charge the battery, which is then channelled to an inverter and connected to an AC bus. Meanwhile, the output of the SPP is directly connected to a Grid Tie Inverter, which is then connected to the AC bus. During the testing phase, both power generations were successfully to supply loads of 20, 25, 30, 35, 40, and 45 Watts. However, when 40 and 45 load were applied, the battery disliked rapidly due battery control unit to slow response of backed up by the MPPT for recharging.

Author Keywords: Utilizes both wind and solar energy

articleTitle: Radiowave Pathloss Modeling Using Polynomial Methods for Wet and Dry Land Adan Rice Agriculture
publicationTitle: 2024 11th International Conference on Electrical Engineering, Computer Science and Informatics (EECSI)
abstract: The high demand for agricultural food to meet human needs continues to increase every year. This triggers the continued advancement of technology in the field of precision agriculture which involves wireless-sensor-network (WSN) to continue to be researched and developed. This technology is believed to provide convenience because it is low cost, high efficiency, high efficiency, and provides high productivity results. WSN takes advantage of advances in the internet and communication systems where this system is very dependent on the availability of internet interconnections. One of the main problems in WSN is the existence of pathloss in the propagation of radio waves from the transmitter (Tx) to the receiver (Rx) which depends on distance, agricultural conditions and the surrounding vegetation environment. This really determines the transmit power between Tx and Rx which ultimately affects the data sent to Rx. This paper provides modeling and analysis of radio wave propagation from RF measurements on the 2.4 GHz WSN system for Adan rice agriculture based on polynomial methods which will modify empirical models such as Free-space, Two-ray, Weissberger, lTU-vegetation, COST-235, and FITU-R involving dry and wet land conditions. Several other factors are also considered in the evaluation and analysis, i.e. the distance and height of the Tx-Rx antenna. The results of the experimental evaluation show that the proposed model, polynomial quadratic and cubic provide the best RMSE for RF system measurements of around 2.32dB and 6.80dB respectively compared to other empirical models.

Index Terms: Lowest Root Mean Square Error Values

articleTitle: Optimization of the Naïve Bayes Algorithm Using Ant Colony Optimization for the Classification of Stroke Patient Data
publicationTitle: 2024 11th International Conference on Electrical Engineering, Computer Science and Informatics (EECSI)
abstract: Stroke is a dangerous disease that is included in the 10 deadliest diseases in Indonesia, with a very high mortality rate. To detect strokes, CT scans and MRI examinations are usually used. However, this examination is expensive and is often only carried out after someone has had a stroke. As a result, medical treatment can be delayed and the patient's condition can worsen. Therefore, it is very important for a method that can identify a patient's condition at an early stage to detect the risk of stroke by classifying whether the patient is experiencing a stroke or not. One method that is often used for classification is Naive Bayes. However, this method has the weakness of passing data into certain classes even though the data is not relevant or relevant so it needs to be optimized by feature selection. From this, optimization was carried out using the Ant Colony Optimization algorithm for feature selection for classification using Naive Bayes. In this research, feature selection will be carried out on the data that will be classified with Naive Bayes using the Ant Colony Optimization algorithm. The accuracy of the Naive Bayes method before and after being optimized with the Ant Colony Optimization algorithm was 86.45% and 95.84% without the use of resampling techniques, while with the application of resampling techniques, the accuracy was 78.69% and 79.91 %.

articleTitle: A Wideband $2\times 2$ Stacked Antenna Array with 9.5 dBi Gain for MMW Applications
publicationTitle: 2024 11th International Conference on Electrical Engineering, Computer Science and Informatics (EECSI)
abstract: This study presents a novel <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$2\times 2$</tex> stacked antenna array that specifically targets Millimeter-wave (MMW) applications. The proposed stacking configuration improves the antenna's bandwidth, where the proposed antenna achieves a bandwidth of 26% at 34.5 GHz. The antenna employs Rogers RO5808 substrate material, with a permittivity of 2.1 and a thickness of 0.787 mm. The antenna operates in the frequency range of 30 to 39 GHz, with a VSWR value of less than 2 across the entire frequency bandwidth and a high peak gain of 9.5 dBi. The proposed antenna exhibits an omnidirectional pattern, offering the advantage of broader coverage. The antenna's compact dimensions and highly effective design make it suitable for integration into various communication systems.

articleTitle: PyStartEase: Enhancing Python Learning for Beginners through Interactive Quizzes and Community Support on a Mobile Platform
publicationTitle: 2024 11th International Conference on Electrical Engineering, Computer Science and Informatics (EECSI)
abstract: PyStartEase is an Android app designed to help beginners, particularly teenagers and school students with no programming background, learn Python effectively. The app employs a quiz-based approach that reinforces understanding through retrieval practice, complemented by explanatory videos and practical examples. PyStartEase also includes a forum for peer collaboration, fostering a community-driven learning environment, and a “Python News!” section to keep users updated with the latest developments in the Python ecosystem. The app's interactive elements cater to different learning styles, and initial user testing suggests a high level of intuitiveness and ease of navigation. Feedback indicates that the app has an engaging interface and effective learning tools, with suggestions for further enhancements such as a code compiler, more interactive content, and gamification elements to boost motivation and engagement. PyStartEase aims to make Python learning more accessible, engaging, and effective for beginners, contributing to the broader goal of making programming knowledge more widespread and approachable.

articleTitle: Method for Determining Node Position in Vehicle Ad-Hoc Network Based on Generator Simulation Urban Mobility (SUMO) Optimization
publicationTitle: 2024 11th International Conference on Electrical Engineering, Computer Science and Informatics (EECSI)
abstract: The development of vehicle ad hoc network (VANET) technology is increasingly developing; this can be achieved because road traffic simulators and network communications are complex and always changing, and a hybrid framework is often required. One hybrid approach is by simulating vehicles in a network, combining Urban Mobility Simulation (SUMO) with OMNET++, which is widely used in discrete simulations, and traffic modeling, which is also used to detect nodes that have experienced losses and are prone to errors. In addition, traffic modeling contributes to traffic recovery, which is very important for developing complex frameworks. This research proposes integrating an extension model as the main contribution to the development of SUMO, which can quickly compare the performance of VANET networks in several scenarios (gridded maps and real maps). This research presents guidelines for fast VANET simulation by producing average values of PDR, packet loss, and end-to-end delay, which is much faster than previous research, so it can be concluded that node movements in the simulation area can be found within 3 seconds.

articleTitle: Implementation of Artificial Intelligence Internet of Things (AIoT) Device for Activity Recognition
publicationTitle: 2024 11th International Conference on Electrical Engineering, Computer Science and Informatics (EECSI)
abstract: With everything being instant nowadays it results in someone without aware of experiencing a lack of movement. This can have a negative impact on health and can cause disease. To overcome this, currently there are many portable devices such as cell phones and smart watches that have functions as an activity monitor. However, it is still limited steps activity, even though human movement activities are not only manifested from steps. One of the problems is because the processing method still relies on processing simple digital signal processing (DSP). Other influencing factors is the processing component (central processing unit, CPU) that is used to have lightweight computing to pursue low device power consumption. This research develops a framework and prototype for custom human activity recognition (HAR) using inertial sensors. The microcontroller is used as a data processing unit so that it can recognize activities carried out. The method that will be used is a combination of digital signal processing and machine learning (ML), as well as equipped with an internet. As evaluation, hardware performance and activity recognition (3 basic table tennis movement) were tested. In the result, device prototype has maximum 245 mA draw current and up to 100% on accuracy of activity recognition. With IoT embed to the device its enable for further development and application usage.

articleTitle: Converging Chaos into Stability through the Integration of the Chua Circuit with Another Circuit
publicationTitle: 2024 11th International Conference on Electrical Engineering, Computer Science and Informatics (EECSI)
abstract: This research investigates the convergence of chaotic dynamics into stability through the integration of the Chua circuit with another circuit. The combination of these circuits is explored to reveal a dynamic transition from chaotic behavior to a stable state. Numerical simulations and analytical methods are employed to elucidate the complex dynamics and understand the factors contributing to the convergence phenomenon. The study not only provides insights into the interaction between the Chua circuit and the supplementary circuitry but also sheds light on the potential applications of such convergence in diverse scientific and engineering fields. The findings contribute to our understanding of complex systems and open avenues for further exploration in nonlinear dynamics and electronic circuit design

articleTitle: Sentiment Analysis of JNT Express, JNE and Sicepat Customer Satisfaction on Twitter Using Multinomial Naïve Bayes Method
publicationTitle: 2024 11th International Conference on Electrical Engineering, Computer Science and Informatics (EECSI)
abstract: The number of online buying and selling transactions through e-commerce as well as the need to deliver personal goods has led to an increase in the number of people using goods delivery services. Goods delivery service companies that are a favorite among Indonesians are JNT Express, JNE and Sicepat. Currently, these companies have been actively using various communication media, including Twitter to interact with their customers. Customer opinions about delivery services often appear on Twitter and sometimes become the main issue that steals the attention until it becomes a headline and becomes a hot conversation among the public. Analyzing customer sentiment through comments on Twitter is very important for JNT Express, JNE, and Sicepat. The Multinomial Naïve Bayes method was used to explore customers' views on their delivery services. A total of 1069 comment data was obtained using Google Collaboratory with the help of tweet-harvest from January 1, 2023 to December 31, 2023. The sentiment classification process was performed by utilizing Naïve Bayes classification to identify whether the reviews are positive, negative, or neutral. The classification results of the dataset with a composition of 75% of the training data and 25% of the test data on the JNT Express expedition obtained an accuracy result of 80%, JNE obtained an accuracy result of 75% and Sicepat 67%. For datasets with 80% and 20% composition, JNT Express obtained an accuracy of 77%, JNE 74% and Sicepat 65%.

articleTitle: Steganography Audio Files Using EAS Method and AES CBC Algorithm for Data Security
publicationTitle: 2024 11th International Conference on Electrical Engineering, Computer Science and Informatics (EECSI)
abstract: The ease of exchanging information can be misused by irresponsible parties to commit various cybercrimes such as data tapping. Therefore, this study was conducted with the aim of creating an Android-based application that is used to secure data. The method used to secure data is a combination of steganography techniques using EAS (Enhanced Audio Steganography) method with cryptography techniques using AES (Advanced Encryption Standard) mode CBC (Cipher Block Chaining) algorithm. Application of steganography is carried out using the EAS method, where data is inserted into certain bytes, so that it can maintain the quality of the cover media used. The cover media used is audio in W A V format. The application of cryptography is carried out using the AES mode CBC algorithm which is a popular symmetric algorithm because of its high performance and level of security. In addition, GZIP compression is also applied to perform data compression which aims to increase the storage capacity of the audio cover. The results of this study are to produce an Android-based application that is used to secure data by inserting data into the audio cover and can be extracted back into the original data.

articleTitle: Implementing a Smart Farm Layer Management System Using Microcontrollers and Android
publicationTitle: 2024 11th International Conference on Electrical Engineering, Computer Science and Informatics (EECSI)
abstract: Cage management has long been considered one of the most important influences on poultry health and productivity. As well as the comfort of the cage, it is important to focus on safety and maintain all conditions in, around, and through equipment and supplies that have been used, implementing a preset condition or an overall system. Nevertheless, the closed-house layer cage system is said to be associated with some disadvantages. For example: There is no real-time capture and recording of temperature and humidity values detected by sensors. Furthermore, although the system includes some real-time values and notifications about egg collections, it does not have any daily recording data or performance dashboard for the cage, for example, indicating eggs laid per day versus the predicted number of chickens in cages, so production efficiency can be calculated on a weekly basis. It is also clear that such attributes will be a requirement for breeders to make continued performance evaluations simpler. Further, there is no layered security system in place to operate the instruments or appliances installed. The existing control system can only be operated within the enclosure on a control panel and does not support remote operation with mobile devices.

articleTitle: Proposed Multi-Pathization Method with SDN for Multiple Paths for TCP Throughput
publicationTitle: 2024 11th International Conference on Electrical Engineering, Computer Science and Informatics (EECSI)
abstract: In this paper, we propose an innovative method to control the increasing traffic volume caused by the proliferation of IoT devices, utilizing Software Defined Networking (SDN). Our method leverages a genetic algorithm, a powerful numerical optimization technique, to determine the optimal forwarding probability that maximizes Quality of Service (QoS) across the network. We experimentally evaluate the TCP throughput of the proposed method under various conditions in a multi-route network topology. The results of these experiments confirm the effectiveness and robustness of our scheme, showing significant improvements in network performance compared to traditional methods. This approach is particularly valuable for future network environments where IoT devices are expected to dominate, providing a scalable solution to manage network congestion and maintain high QoS standards. The potential applications of our method extend to various IoT-driven industries, making it a crucial tool for network administrators in the era of ubiquitous connectivity.

articleTitle: RFID-Based Smart Secure E-Bike Parking Station
publicationTitle: 2024 11th International Conference on Electrical Engineering, Computer Science and Informatics (EECSI)
abstract: This research discusses the safety challenges faced by bicycle smart parking systems, which are often irregular and unsafe, especially in Indonesia. The purpose of this research is to develop an RFID-based smart parking system for electric bicycles that improves user safety and accessibility. The system is designed using components such as the NodeMCU 8266 microcontroller, RFID module, and solenoid lock, and is tested under real-world conditions. Using the <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$\mathrm{C}++$</tex> programming language to be embedded in a microcontroller. Quantitative results show that the system achieved an 80% success rate in RFID detection on various materials with optimal performance through acrylic barriers. The system demonstrates better safety compared to traditional bicycle parking solutions, which contributes to increased public confidence in the safety of electric bicycles.

articleTitle: Dimensional Analysis of Charge Carrier Mobility in Organic Semiconductors
publicationTitle: 2024 11th International Conference on Electrical Engineering, Computer Science and Informatics (EECSI)
abstract: Organic semiconductors have gained attention due to their flexibility. A key property of these materials is charge mobility, which is crucial for determining the speed at which charges, such as electrons and holes, move within solid. Consequently, understanding and accurately modeling charge mobility is essential for optimizing the performance of organic semiconductors. From the reference numerical equations, we have determined the charge carrier mobility through the dimensional analysis method. To obtain the charge mobility values, regression was used from synthetic data. In theory, charge mobility in organic semiconductors is a hopping transport in disordered systems with Gaussian energy distribution. The results showed good agreement with the reference model. It can be concluded that the dimensional analysis method is applicable to observe charge carrier mobility.

articleTitle: A Comparative Analysis of Snort and Dendritic Cell Algorithm in Intrusion Detection Systems
publicationTitle: 2024 11th International Conference on Electrical Engineering, Computer Science and Informatics (EECSI)
abstract: In this study, we compare the performance of snort and dendritic cell algorithm (DCA) as intrusion detection systems (IDS) based on several key metrics. The evaluation results show that DCA has a higher true positive rate (TPR) of 99.8% compared to snort which only reached 71.85%, indicating that DCA is more effective in detecting true positive. However, DCA also has a higher false positive rate (FPR) of 20.03% compared to snort's 1.97%, indicating that DCA tends to generate more false alarms. As a result of the high FPR, the overall accuracy of DCA (84.45%) is lower than snort (89.2%). Additionally, DCA evaluates a larger sample size (37,801) than Snort (27,227), indicating that DCA handles more data or cases in this evaluation. In conclusion, although DCA is superior in true positive detection, snort is more reliable in generating accurate alarms with fewer false alarms. The integration of these two methods can provide an optimal solution by exploiting the high sensitivity of DCA and the reliability of snort.

articleTitle: A Wheat Grain Variety Recognition Based on Deep Learning
publicationTitle: 2024 11th International Conference on Electrical Engineering, Computer Science and Informatics (EECSI)
abstract: This study introduces a deep learning-based approach to wheat grain variety recognition, a critical task for enhancing wheat quality and yield. It details the creation of a wheat kernel image dataset, capturing images from multiple angles of 22 varieties, followed by preprocessing steps to standardize and prepare the data for analysis. The study leverages convolutional neural networks (CNNs) and transfer learning to develop a model capable of identifying wheat varieties with high accuracy, addressing the limitations of traditional machine learning methods. The results demonstrate the superiority of deep learning in wheat kernel identification, with the optimized moachieving a remarkable recognition rate of 99.3%. This high performance is attributed to the ability of CNN s to automatically extract features and learn from the data, thus eliminating the need for manual feature engineering.

articleTitle: Application Quality Trial for Formative-Summative Assessment Utilizing WP-TP
publicationTitle: 2024 11th International Conference on Electrical Engineering, Computer Science and Informatics (EECSI)
abstract: The purpose of this study was to present the findings from the Formative-Summative assessment application based on WP-TP (Weighted Product-Tri Pramana) quality trials. This application used the Form ative-Summ ative assessment paradigm, the WP (Weighted Product) decision support technique, and the idea of TP (Tri Pramana), a term for traditional Balinese knowledge. The methodology for this investigation was quantitative. Ten professionals/experts served as test subjects for the application quality. Experts utilized a questionnaire as a tool to evaluate the quality of application. A quantitative descriptive technique was employed to examine the application quality testing outcomes. Using an eleven-point scale as a guide, this technique evaluated the application quality trial results with quality criteria. The application quality was good, as seen by the average percentage of 85.818%. The research's findings will advance the area of education by creating a new type of artificial intelligence-based assessment tool for comprehensive, accurate, and clear evaluation of educational policies and programs.

articleTitle: Comparative Study of Two and Three Level Inverter to Control Three-Phase Induction Machine Based on DTC
publicationTitle: 2024 11th International Conference on Electrical Engineering, Computer Science and Informatics (EECSI)
abstract: This study presents a design and interpretation of the Direct Torque Control (DTC) technology for controlling the induction motors(IM). The conventional form of this technology has several disadvantages. Power electronics presents greater flexibility in achieving the desired output power due to its numerous advantages. As a result, this study utilizes a three-level inverter with neutral clamping point (NPC) technology. The findings of this study indicated that using DTC technology with a three-level inverter gives less torque ripple, improvement of stator flux and reduces the harmonics in the stator current, preventing motor body vibration. In addition, comparisons between the two techniques were obtained using the MATLAB/Simulink environment in this study.

articleTitle: Harmonic Analysis of PV Inverter-Based EV Charging Station Activity on the Utility Grid
publicationTitle: 2024 11th International Conference on Electrical Engineering, Computer Science and Informatics (EECSI)
abstract: The use of electric vehicles (EV) is increasing day by day due to the commitment of various countries to reduce carbon emissions from the use of conventional vehicles based on fossil fuels. The use of solar energy at EV charging stations will reduce carbon emissions more significantly compared to the public grid which is still dominated by coal fuel at present. The development of EV charging stations integration with the grid and photovoltaic (PV) PV inverter can cause power quality problems such as harmonics. This is due to the use of DC/AC or AC/DC converters on the PV EV charging station side which contains distortion in the voltage and current waveform. In this paper, the effect of adding PV inverter-based electric vehicle charging stations to an electric power distribution network is presented. The simulation results show that there is an increase in current and voltage harmonics with the use of a PV inverter compared to a charging system using a grid.

articleTitle: Green Transportation Route Model for Industrial Goods Delivery with Genetic Algorithm
publicationTitle: 2024 11th International Conference on Electrical Engineering, Computer Science and Informatics (EECSI)
abstract: The urgency of goods delivery activities in routine and important industries has the potential to damage the environment, high transportation costs and delays in goods delivery. In an effort to handle complex problems, it is necessary to determine routes considering distance and time to different locations in order to get the best green transportation route. The data used are manufacturing industry latitude and longitude coordinate point data from factory data, distributor data and shop/retailer data. Next, the data is processed using Extract Transform Load (ETL) with Google Collab Tool Python to get the best new distance used in the green transportation route determination model. The aim of the research is to design a green transportation route model using a genetic algorithm. The benefits of research are it can provide information for industry in determining the best route, thereby making delivery of goods to consumers more effective and transport costs efficient; Can optimize green transportation routes reducing the impact of pollution resulting from shipping goods; The research method is a green transportation route model with a genetic algorithm. The results of this research produced a green transportation route model with a genetic algorithm for the Palembang factory to the distributor with the best distence 272.443766121975, the Baturaja factory to the distributor best distence 272.4437714642356, and from the Lampung factory to the distributor best distence 272.4437512424067.

articleTitle: Vehicle Routing Problem with Time Windows using Hybrid Metaheuristic Dragonfly Algorithm and Variable Neighborhood Search: Work on Progress
publicationTitle: 2024 11th International Conference on Electrical Engineering, Computer Science and Informatics (EECSI)
abstract: One of the problems with Smart Transportation is the problem of cost and travel time. This problem is known as the Variable Routing Problem (VRP). In some real cases, in addition to considering route selection, there are limitations on the capacity and time period for the vehicle to serve each customer known as Time Windows, so VRP has developed into Variable Routing Problem with Time Windows (VRPTW). One way to solve VRPTW is to use metaheuristic methods. However, the metaheuristic method has a weakness, which are it can get stuck in local optimums and fail to find better global solutions. To overcome this, a combination with other methods or known as hybrid is needed. The formulation of this research problem is how to develop a Smart transportation model using a metaheuristic hybrid algorithm. The purpose of this study is to develop a Smart transportation model using a metaheuristic hybrid algorithm. The method used is to combine two metaheuristic algorithms, which are the Dragonfly Algorithm (DA) and the Variable Neighborhood Search (VNS). The result of this research is a new algorithm model which is a hybrid between DA and VNS. Through a combination of global exploration using DA and local exploitation using VNS, this algorithm is expected to be able to find a better solution and faster convergence in solving VRPTW problems

Author Keywords: variable routing problem with time windows

articleTitle: K-Nearest Neighbor Classification Based on Gas Array Sensor to Detect Borax in Meatballs
publicationTitle: 2024 11th International Conference on Electrical Engineering, Computer Science and Informatics (EECSI)
abstract: Borax is a white powder consisting of colorless crystals and easily soluble in water. This chemical can also be used to separate gold from ore to replace the use of mercury. It is very dangerous if chemicals such as borax are used illegally and mixed into processed foods such as meatballs and eaten by humans continuously over a long period of time. The use of borax as a preservative in food is difficult to recognize with the naked eye. The test that is usually carried out to see the borax content in food is a laboratory test. So it is necessary to apply technology to overcome this problem. In recent years, a lot of research has been carried out to identify borax levels in food, one of which is by using a series of gas sensors as an electronic smell (e-nose). The focus of this research is to detect processed meatball foods that contain borax by classifying them using the KNN method and using the Enose sensor series based on gas sensors from the Figaro manufacturer, namely the TGS gas sensor series. The TGS gas sensor response combined with the K-Nearest Neighbor (KNN) method shows that the sensor can classification the gas in meatballs with and without borax into two types. Determining the number of neighbors (K) that will be used to consider class determination. The research results obtained an accuracy value of 100% for K=1, K=3, K=5 and K=9 and 90% for K=11.

articleTitle: Classifying the Size of Shallots Using Watershed Transformation Algorithm
publicationTitle: 2024 11th International Conference on Electrical Engineering, Computer Science and Informatics (EECSI)
abstract: This study aims to detect shallots that are close together and their classification based on diameter. The proposed system uses images taken from a moving conveyor belt with a distance between the camera and the object of 25 cm and a speed of 40 rpm with a frame rate of 30 fps and a resolution of 1920 × 1080 pixels. The total data used in this study is 267 frames, researchers divide it into 70% for training data and 30% for testing data. This research implements watershed transform segmentation for segmenting shallot images that are close together, then implements the bounding box method to detect shallots based on the results of segmentation and feature extraction using the pixel per centimeter ratio formula to calculate the diameter of shallots then classify them according to their diameter. The test results of this research provide a limitation for the bounding box area to be used. Blob areas that are less than 100 will not be labeled for the bounding box of the detected object. The training data value for RMSE is 0.292, and MAPE is 6.290%, while the testing results with video data produce an RMSE of 0.176 and MAPE of 3.507%. The MAPE value below 10% demonstrates that the model exhibits excellent performance in measuring shallots diameter.

articleTitle: Cross-Site Scripting (XSS) Vulnerabilities in Modern Web Applications
publicationTitle: 2024 11th International Conference on Electrical Engineering, Computer Science and Informatics (EECSI)
abstract: The storage of information on websites and the internet facilitates user data exchange. However, only those with authorization can access the content. Unauthorized parties also become interested in the vast amount of information available on the internet. Unauthorized parties employ various methods to gain access and information. One of them is caused by a cross-site scripting attack. This attack specifically targets the website. Understanding this type of attack is crucial for web-based information system developers, as it exploits weaknesses in programming or code writing within the information system. The results of this test found that 40% of websites were vulnerable to XSS attacks with the type are Reflected and DOM Based Attack

articleTitle: An Enhanced Method with Part of Speech Tagging and Named Entity Recognition Techniques Towards Advanced Persistent Threat in Cyber Threat Intelligence: Work in Progress
publicationTitle: 2024 11th International Conference on Electrical Engineering, Computer Science and Informatics (EECSI)
abstract: This research enhances the development of natural language processing (NLP) by integrating part of speech (POS) tagging and named entity recognition (NER) techniques to annotate unstructured data from advanced persistent threat (APT) news. This paper uses combination of these two techniques with deep learning methods, specifically bidirectional long short-term memory (BiLSTM) and conditional random field (CRF) to automate data annotation. The objective is to automatically convert the unstructured APT data into structured threat information expression (STIX) format. The proposed approach can be further developed into cyber threat intelligence (CTI) system for information exchange and early warning against cybercrime. This research is currently in the preliminary stage with progress including data collection and preprocessing, and BiLSTM model building. The expected outcome is a model that capable of APT data labeling to enhance CTI systems.

articleTitle: SQL and NoSQL Object-Database Mapping Using Property Graphs in Relational Cases
publicationTitle: 2024 11th International Conference on Electrical Engineering, Computer Science and Informatics (EECSI)
abstract: This paper discusses the inherent challenges of SQL and NoSQL object mapping, primarily focusing on the heterogeneity of data models and its impact on database relationship. In NoSQL databases, relationships between entities can be defined using references or embedded objects. Each method has its advantages and trade-offs, and different NoSQL DBMS adopt different strategies based on their design principles and use cases. We examine how different SQL Database Management Systems (DBMS) handle relationships between entities, specifically comparing the use of embedded objects in MongoDB with the graph-based reference system in Neo4J. Object mapping is built using property graphs that represent the schema in the database. The framework was tested using the hospital information system medical record module. The results of this study show that the object mapping that has been built can run query commands on three distinct types of databases: MySQL, MongoDB, and Neo4j.

articleTitle: Evaluating the Effectiveness of Multiple Machine Learning Models in Date Fruit Recognition
publicationTitle: 2024 11th International Conference on Electrical Engineering, Computer Science and Informatics (EECSI)
abstract: - This study evaluates the efficacy of various machine learning models in classifying date fruits. The objective was to determine the most effective model using comprehensive performance indicators, including AUC, CA, F1, Precision, Recall, and MCC. We employed Random Forest, SVM, Gradient Boosting, AdaBoost, Naive Bayes, and kNN models on a dataset sourced from Kaggle. The results demonstrate that the Gradient Boosting model outperforms others, achieving the highest values in AUC (0.992), CA (0.922), Fl (0.920), Precision (0.927), Recall (0.922), and MCC (0.907). While SVM and Random Forest also showed robust performance, Gradient Boosting established itself as the most reliable for this classification task. However, the study's limitations include the dataset's scope and the specific focus on date fruits. Future research should incorporate additional features and advanced techniques, and validate these models across various agricultural products to enhance generalizability.

articleTitle: Comparative Study of Facial Expression Recognition Using Facial Landmark in e-Learning System
publicationTitle: 2024 11th International Conference on Electrical Engineering, Computer Science and Informatics (EECSI)
abstract: The e-Iearning system or distance learning system has become important, especially during the COVID-19 pan-demic. Several tertiary institutions have made the e-Iearning system an alternative teaching and learning activity. Research on the use of e-Iearning needs to be explored to obtain innovative, creative, and fun learning. One aspect that can be examined in e-learning is students' emotional response to the learning activities. The emotional state of students directly or indirectly affects the learning process. The student's emotional responses can be measured by their facial expressions. In this study, an exploration was carried out on the facial expressions shown by students in HSS Learning, an e-Iearning for learning web programming. The student's facial expressions were extracted using 68 pairs of facial landmarks and additional 6 facial feature vectors. The total number of features used is 142. Machine learning methods for classification are applied to determine the performance of several classification models, including the k-Nearest Neighbor (k- NN) algorithm, Logistic Regression, and Support Vector Machine (SVM). Machine learning performance evaluation is done using the Fl-score and confusion matrix. The results show that the accuracy of the k-NN, Logistic Regression, and SVM are 91.4%, 92.2%, and 92.1 %, respectively. However, the Fl-score macro values are relatively low due to data imbalance with the k- NN, Logistic Regression, and SVM models are 0.250, 0.272, and 0.243, respectively. While the study provides insight into the student learning experience in e-Iearning settings, this study needs to be explored more.

articleTitle: Determination of Harmonic Filter Effect on Single-Phase Residential Energy Meter
publicationTitle: 2024 11th International Conference on Electrical Engineering, Computer Science and Informatics (EECSI)
abstract: This study examines the impact of the use of non-linear loads in household installations with 450 VA power on harmonic distortion and accuracy of kWh meter readings, both analog and digital. Using hardware such as LIPUVINDO LPV 510520 Analog kWh Meter, HUABANG Digital kWh Meter, HIOKI 3197 Power Quality Analyzer, and OMRON H5-CX Timer, as well as loads in the form of incandescent lamps, LEDs, LHE, monitors, chargers, and 1-phase motors, the study found that harmonic distortion can cause kWh meter reading errors of up to 9,83% at 450 VA loads. The accuracy of the kWh meter is very important because a small error can cause losses to both consumers and manufacturers. The data shows that the greater the THDI (Total Harmonic Distortion Current) value, the greater the error of the kWh meter reading, with the percentage of error reaching 2,54% on digital kWh meters and 9,837% on analog kWh meters for 450 VA loads. This study emphasizes the importance of taking into account the load to maintain the quality of power in household installations, especially in low-voltage installations that are widely used in Indonesia.

articleTitle: Black Hole Attacks Detection in Mobile Ad Hoc Networks (MANETs) using Bayesian Inference Method
publicationTitle: 2024 11th International Conference on Electrical Engineering, Computer Science and Informatics (EECSI)
abstract: MANET has vulnerability in terms of security systems against black hole attacks. The main target of black hole as a malicious node is to absorbs all data. The aim of this research is to identify black hole attacks against MANE Tusing Bayesian inference. The methodology of this research involves several testing phases. In the first phase, all data packets sent by the source node to destination within the range of the black hole node are lost. The second and third testing phases showed that the Bayesian method was successful in detecting black holes by preventing data transmission. The results indicated that traffic in the MANET runs smoothly when the nodes are operating under normal conditions. However, when a black hole node is introduced, a significant number of data packets are lost. Implementing the Bayesian method offers a solution to this issue.

articleTitle: A Routing Algorithm Based on Node Centrality and Optimal Stop Rule in Mobile Opportunistic Networks
publicationTitle: 2024 11th International Conference on Electrical Engineering, Computer Science and Informatics (EECSI)
abstract: In the mobile opportunity network, the forwarding mechanism with multiple copies is usually used to accelerate the spread of information, but it will also lead to the aggravation of network overload. How to reduce network overhead under the premise of ensuring a high delivery rate and low delay is an important research direction in mobile opportunistic networks. Firstly, in order to avoid the problem of excessive number of replicas in the network, this paper determines the optimal initial number of copies based on the optimal stop rule. Then, aiming at the problem of inefficient allocation of copy numbers in the process of data forwarding, we proposed a routing algorithm based on node centrality. Finally, through simulation experiments, and the results show that the algorithm achieves higher delivery rate, lower delay and network overhead compared with others.

articleTitle: Priority Based Cyber Incident Handling: Work in Progress
publicationTitle: 2024 11th International Conference on Electrical Engineering, Computer Science and Informatics (EECSI)
abstract: Effective and efficient cyber incident handling is crucial for maintaining the security of information systems and organizational data. This research aims to develop a priority-based cyber incident handling method by adopting the NIST 2.0 framework and utilizing machine learning classification algorithms. This method enables organizations to quickly and accurately identify and respond to incidents based on threat levels and impact, focusing resources on the most critical incidents. The research employs the Support Vector Machine (SVM) classification algorithm to determine incident priorities. The study is still developing for handling cyber incidents, followed by testing and evaluating the system prototype within organizations. Initial results indicate that the priority-based approach using the SVM classification algorithm achieves a True Positive (TP) Rate of 0.999 and a False Positive (FP) Rate of 0.008, with a correlation of 98.88%, resulting in excellent performance in identifying positive cases and a low error rate.

articleTitle: Design of Saturated Core Fault Current Limiter for Integration of Electrical Power Supply
publicationTitle: 2024 11th International Conference on Electrical Engineering, Computer Science and Informatics (EECSI)
abstract: There was an issue with the PLN and Genset synchronization system in the XYZ Factory electrical power system. The two power sources could not be safely synchronized because the short circuit current value on the main bus during the power PLN and Genset electrical power synchronization exceeded the main bus's short circuit current capacity. This research solves the problems that occur by installing a limiting reactor. The approach method is carried out with the help of ETAP 19.0.1 software as a model of the factory electrical power system. This research begins by analyzing the value of the short circuit current on the main bus when the two power sources are synchronized, then looking for the reactance value of the short circuit current limiting reactor. Short circuit current limiting reactors can reduce short circuit current values with 3-phase fault types from 77.034 kA to 55.898 kA, Line to Ground fault types from 80.268 kA to 41.798 kA, Line to Line fault types from 67.326 kA to 48.41 kA, and Double Line to Ground fault type from 79.121 kA to 54.009 kA.

articleTitle: Determinants of Mobile-Assisted Language Learning Continuance Intention: Extending TCT with Gamification and Trust
publicationTitle: 2024 11th International Conference on Electrical Engineering, Computer Science and Informatics (EECSI)
abstract: Mobile-assisted language learning (MALL) is an alternative medium that enhances the flexibility and accessibility of foreign language learning. Looking at MALL“ s positive reception and growing popularity in Indonesia., a critical challenge remains: identifying factors of users” continuance intention. This research will complement past studies on the continuous intention to use MALL., applying the Technology Continuance Theory (TCT) extended with gamification and trust. A total of 342 valid samples were gathered through Google Forms between late April and mid-May 2024., targeting active MALL users in Indonesia. The samples were then further analyzed using SmartPLS 4.0. Results have shown that trust., satisfaction., attitude., and gamification have an influential impact on the users” continuous intention to use MALL. However., two of 14 hypotheses were thus rejected., specifically perceived ease of use toward attitude in using MALL and perceived usefulness toward MALL continuance intention.

articleTitle: Detection and Classification of Skin Cancer Using YOLOv8n
publicationTitle: 2024 11th International Conference on Electrical Engineering, Computer Science and Informatics (EECSI)
abstract: Skin cancer is a disease caused by the growth of abnormal cells in skin tissues. The World Health Organization (WHO) has recorded an 88% increase in deaths due to skin cancer caused by exposure to ultraviolet rays. Currently, in the medical field, the diagnosis of skin cancer involves a biopsy process, which requires considerable time and cost. Therefore, this study aims to develop a system for detecting and classifying skin cancer based on the shape of skin lesions using the You Only Look Once version 8 nano (YOLOv8n), which can detect lesions rapidly. The dataset used is ISIC 2019, comprising of 4289 images of cancerous skin lesions divided into 9 classes: Basal Cell Carcinoma, Squamous Cell Carcinoma, Melanoma, Actinic Keratosis, Dermatofibroma, Nevus, Seborrheic Keratosis, Pigmented Benign Keratosis, and Vascular Lesion. Experimental results show that the designed system performs well in detecting and classifying the lesions, achieving an overall accuracy of 93.5%, with a Precision of 93.5%, Recall of 93.7<sup xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">%</sup>, and an F1-Score of 93.5%.

articleTitle: Classifier Optimization with a Test-Time Training Layer for Employee Attrition Prediction
publicationTitle: 2024 11th International Conference on Electrical Engineering, Computer Science and Informatics (EECSI)
abstract: Employee attrition poses significant challenges for organizations, impacting productivity and increasing recruitment costs. This paper presents an innovative approach to optimize baseline classifiers by integrating a Test-Time Training (TTT) layer. The proposed method refines model predictions on unseen data, enhancing adaptability to new patterns in employee behavior. We evaluate the performance of the optimized model using the IBM Analytics HR Employee Attrition dataset, which includes 1,470 observations and 34 features. The dataset was split into training and test sets, with 80% of the data used for training and 20% for testing. The results demonstrate that incorporating a TTT layer significantly improves prediction accuracy compared to the baseline Logistic Regression model, the SVM model and the Random Forest model with notable enhancements in metrics such as accuracy, precision, and F1-score. These findings suggest that this approach provides organizations with a robust tool for predicting employee attrition.

articleTitle: Measuring Data Quality In Higher Education By Using Loshin's Framework
publicationTitle: 2024 11th International Conference on Electrical Engineering, Computer Science and Informatics (EECSI)
abstract: University is an educational unit that organizes state higher education. According to the law of the Republic of Indonesia article No. 12 of 2012 stipulates that higher education organizers must collect, compile and send data on higher education organizations to pddikti, to ensure their completeness, accuracy, authenticity and updated version. Therefore, until now the University has not been able to fully meet the demands of the regulation. This problem is a concern for management, because reporting data to that organization is a national standard for higher education that must be met and the information that has been collected will be a source of information for accreditation institutions to accredit study programs and universities while for the public to find out the performance of study programs and universities. According to that problem, this study aims to help overcome problems related to data quality at University by measuring the level of maturity of data quality so that it can be identified which areas need to be improved. The measurement phases use David Loshin's Data Quality Framework, which evaluates 8 domains. The measurement results are meant to be used as a guide for making enhancements in order to enhance the quality of basic education data.

articleTitle: Internet of Things-Based Early Forest Fire Detection System with Thinger.io Platform
publicationTitle: 2024 11th International Conference on Electrical Engineering, Computer Science and Informatics (EECSI)
abstract: Forest and land fires in Indonesia are a major concern for the government when entering the dry season. The researchers have widely developed early detection technology, including satellite and airborne-based technology, but it faces several limitations due to the influence of weather and other unavoidable factors. Furthermore, fire detection technology based on wireless sensor networks (WSNs) and the Internet of Things (loT) is one of the most effective solutions. This study developed a sensor node that includes an Arduino UNO, a smoke sensor, a fire sensor, and temperature and humidity sensors and code program using C++, to detect potential forest fires. We place these nodes at fire-prone points in the forest. Additionally, the gateway node receive data from the sensor node, process it using the NodeMCU ESP8266, and send it to the Thinger.io database for real-time report. The developed system's test results demonstrate that it can display and send data in real-time to the Thinger.io platform via an internet connection. Additionally, the base station's physical 12C 20x4 LCD screen displays the information. The forest fire early warning system functions well, and the test results show good detection and data transmission capabilities.

articleTitle: Modified CNN Architecture for Paddy Leaf Disease Detection
publicationTitle: 2024 11th International Conference on Electrical Engineering, Computer Science and Informatics (EECSI)
abstract: Paddy (rice) is the main food for the Indonesian people so that stable production is needed to meet domestic needs. However, data in 2023 showed a decline in rice production in Indonesia. The decline was due to pests and diseases that attacked rice plants. The lack of experience and knowledge of farmers in handling and detecting rice diseases is also a factor in the decline in rice productivity. This study aims to develop a computer-aided diagnosis (CAD) system for rice leaf diseases based on CNN algorithms. In creating CAD applications, this study proposes a new CNN architecture based on a modification of the MobileNetV3 architecture. The dataset used comes from direct data collection from rice fields in Indonesia which is then added with public data from Kaggle data totalling 6933 rice leaf images. Based on the results obtained, this study succeeded in surpassing the previous research benchmark with an average accuracy, precision, recall and F -1 Score value reaching 93%.

articleTitle: Satellite Image Denoising Using Deep Learning: Autoencoder Decoder Application
publicationTitle: 2024 11th International Conference on Electrical Engineering, Computer Science and Informatics (EECSI)

authors.preferredName: Sean Chris Kirk Patrick P. Cruz

abstract: Through deep learning Autoencoder Decoders, it is possible to clean noisy or damaged image data received from satellites. Two models with a PSNR of 25.6 dB and 25.54 dB were generated using a dataset consisting of 610 weather satellite images retrieved from the National Oceanic and Atmospheric Administration (NOAA) Weather (WX) satellites. These images were acquired via the ground station at the University of Perpetual Help System DALTA - Las Pinas campus. Initially, only a few alterations were made to the code in order to work with later Keras versions. However, this led to crashes during training as well as noticeable darkening in the predictions. The original code also used accuracy as the training metric, instead of PSNR. The rewrite rebuilt the model using updated Keras 3 API as well as introduced a PSNR metric. Doing so eliminated the darkening and crashes entirely.

articleTitle: Effects of Sparkling Water Stimulation on Gastric Electrical Response Activity
publicationTitle: 2024 11th International Conference on Electrical Engineering, Computer Science and Informatics (EECSI)
abstract: Electrogastrography (EGG) is a non-invasive and affordable measurement technique that measured the myoelectric activity of the stomach using a surface electrode placed on the surface skin of the stomach area. Gastric myoelectric activity (GEA) consists of two main components, namely slow waves or Electrical Control Activity (ECA) and potential spikes or Electrical Response Activity (ERA). The ECA range frequency is normally between 2 to 4 cycles per minute (cpm) with an increase in amplitude after meals. Sparkling water has been shown to be useful in treating gastrointestinal issues. This study aims to investigate the effects of sparkling water stimulation on ERA based on EGG approach. EGG recording were made with three-channel unipolar in a standardized environment and sparkling water were used for ingestion stimulation. Ten healthy participants with no digestive problems were recruited for this study. Initially, the recording was divided into three periods i.e. fasting, postprandial 1, and postprandial 2 with 10 min recording time for each period. EGG signal analyses were processed using Welch Power Spectral Density Analysis based on Fast Fourier transform (FFT). After sparkling water stimulation, there is a significant difference in the first postprandial periods with <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$\mathrm{p} < 0.05$</tex> for ECA dominant frequency (DF). The dominant power (DP) showed an increase but no significant difference was indicated. Moreover, on ERA range frequency the results were surprisingly shown there are significant increases with <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$\mathrm{p} < 0.01$</tex> in both postprandial periods. Our result suggests that ERA reflection was induced by sparkling water stimulation and is solely responsible for gastric motility.

articleTitle: Blockchain Technology Model to Increase Transparency in Sales Transactions in Accounting Information Systems
publicationTitle: 2024 11th International Conference on Electrical Engineering, Computer Science and Informatics (EECSI)
abstract: An accounting system is a series of procedures and methods used to record, process, and report the financial transactions of an institution. Problems arise when companies with partners or subsidiaries integrate financial data and information, but companies with partners use different accounting system platforms. It is very difficult to integrate transactions and information from several different accounting system platforms. Thus, the purpose of this research is to adopt blockchain technology for transactions in the accounting system. Blockchain technology requires every transaction involving parties in the accounting system to go through a peer-to-peer validation process that ensures the transparency of each transaction. The concept of distributed storage in blockchain technology will increase the security of transactions in the accounting system. This research focuses on discussing transactions for purchasing goods from suppliers and selling goods to distributors, which are the initial stages of the accounting system. The research will also discuss blockchain technology-based buying and selling transactions and their relationship to the stages in the next accounting system. The research uses a qualitative approach through a literature review of the phenomena and problems of conventional accounting systems. A literature review is also used to study the conceptual model of blockchain technology with the accounting system in previous research as a reference for creating a proposed model. The research output is a proposed model and simulation with the Hyperledger framework.

articleTitle: Motor Imagery Recognition Using Filter Bank Common Spatial Pattern and Recurrent Neural Networks
publicationTitle: 2024 11th International Conference on Electrical Engineering, Computer Science and Informatics (EECSI)
abstract: A Brain-Computer Interface (BCI) technology allows a person to communicate with hardware without involving physical movement. The instrument that connects brain commands to device movements is called an intermediate, one of which is an Electroencephalogram (EEG). EEG captures brain signals by placing electrodes on the scalp and translating the recorded signals to external commands. In BCI, one of the variables that can be used is motor imagery (MI), where a person can control an external device by imagining its movements. EEG signal processing is important in BCI performance. There are feature extraction and classification. This paper proposed the Common Spatial Pattern (FBCSP) technique for feature extraction and Recurrent Neural Network (RNN) to recognize BCI competition data sets. FBCSP is effective in MI recognition because it extracts frequency and spatial features. RNN is used for the classification by considering the data sequence of each spatial feature of FBCSP extraction. The experiment result showed that of the 9 dataset subjects, the accuracy of each subject is 94.25%, 87.36%, 94.25%, 90.80%, 85.06%, 89.66%, 95.40%, 95.40%, and 93.10, with an average accuracy of 91.69%. If all subject data is combined, the accuracy is 89.97%.

articleTitle: Study on Appropriate Configuration of IEEE 802. 1TSN on Ethernet-Based Industrial Networks
publicationTitle: 2024 11th International Conference on Electrical Engineering, Computer Science and Informatics (EECSI)
abstract: This paper studies a numerical optimization method to find an appropriate configuration in CBS of IEEE 802. 1TSN and compares the obtained results with those of TAS. The authors' previous studies have proposed a method for finding an appropriate TAS GCL in industrial networks using numerical optimization. However, whether the proposal is also effective in the configuration of CBS is still being determined. This paper utilizes the above method to derive the parameter configuration when CBS and TAS are applied to each switch, respectively, by simulation. The experimental results show that the method found the most appropriate configuration in CBS. However, CBS fails to satisfy the delay constraints, whereas TAS does, indicating that TAS can meet more stringent delay constraints.

articleTitle: Design of Servo Control System on Robot Hand Fingers
publicationTitle: 2024 11th International Conference on Electrical Engineering, Computer Science and Informatics (EECSI)
abstract: Robot arms commonly used in the industrial sector are typically controlled using. ioysticks, although this method is not very effective. This project aims to improve control by developing a two-system control setup for the robot arm, focusing on finger and arm control using gloves equipped with bending sensors to detect finger curvature and an inertial measurement unit (IMU) sensor to gauge hand movement direction. The linear actuators control the robot fingers, while Dynamixel smart servo motors control the robot arms. The system utilizes PID control for its control method. Testing the robot hand fingers control system revealed a good response, with an average delay of 0.3 seconds and an average error of 1.44°. Overall testing showed that the robot arm can move based on the set point given by the glove.

articleTitle: Performance Analysis of Single Ended Primary Inductor Converter with Adaptive and Static Proportional Integral Control Variants
publicationTitle: 2024 11th International Conference on Electrical Engineering, Computer Science and Informatics (EECSI)
abstract: The Single-Ended Primary-Inductor Converter (SEPIC) is one type of DC-DC converter that has been widely utilized. In certain conditions, this DC-DC converter may exhibit inappropriate behavior regarding stability and reliability, thus requiring a controller to ensure that the voltage, current, or power values they produce align with the desired one. In this research, we examine and simulate the performance of the SEPIC converter using a Proportional Integral (PI) controller and compare the use of tuning methods: Ziegler-Nichols (ZN), Genetic Algorithm (GA), Particle Swarm Optimization (PSO), and Fuzzy Logic in regulating the PI control parameters. Simulations will be performed through MATLAB. From the simulation results, it is observed that the PI tuning methods using GA, PSO, and Fuzzy Logic are superior to the ZN method, and with the advantage of adaptive process for PI tuning, the fuzzy logic method outperforms in terms of convenience to the other three methods.

articleTitle: Design and Implementation of a Tilapia (Oreochromis niloticus) Fingerling Counter Using Otsu Thresholding and Morphological Transformation Techniques
publicationTitle: 2024 11th International Conference on Electrical Engineering, Computer Science and Informatics (EECSI)
abstract: Many different image processing techniques have been developed and implemented in counting systems for livestock and fisheries applications. These existing systems often require sophisticated hardware and computational resources, leading to an increase in the financial costs associated with their production. In this paper, an innovative Tilapia (Oreochromis niloticus) fingerling counting system is described. The system is comprised of low-cost computer vision-based hardware and software that integrates Otsu thresholding and morphological transformation techniques. These techniques derive contours from segmented regions generated by the formulated algorithms. It uses a Raspberry Pi 4B single-board computer platform in conjunction with a Raspberry Pi Camera Module version 1.3 to capture images. The performance of the manual process and the proposed method were evaluated by determining its mean squared error using a ground truth as a reference. Based on the tests performed, it was revealed that the proposed automatic counting system resulted in a better performance than the manual counting method.

articleTitle: Facial Expression Classification Using Extreme Learning Machine and Genetic Algorithm
publicationTitle: 2024 11th International Conference on Electrical Engineering, Computer Science and Informatics (EECSI)
abstract: Feature extraction is a critical component of facial expression recognition, requiring careful selection to ensure optimal performance. Traditional template-based models often struggle with computational efficiency and are sensitive to factors such as illumination, color variation, and image quality. Although geometry-based models have demonstrated robustness in feature extraction, further optimization remains needed to enhance the recognition accuracy. In this study, the CK+ dataset is utilized, and employ facial landmarks as a geometry-based feature extraction method. The extracted features are then processed using an Extreme Learning Machine combined with Genetic Algorithms (ELM-GA) to select a subset of features and classify facial expressions. The proposed model effectively reduces the number of features used in the classification model by more than half, improving computational efficiency. Additionally, the accuracy of the proposed model outperforms the VGGNet and combination of machine learning and Local Binary Patterns (LBP) and machine learning and Gray-Level Co-occurrence Matrix (GLCM) for feature extraction. Although the current model does not represent the best possible solution, the promising accuracy results provide a solid foundation for further refinement and development in facial expression recognition systems.

articleTitle: Revealing the Potential of Hotel Improvements in Bali Based on Sentiment Analysis and Tourist Characteristics
publicationTitle: 2024 11th International Conference on Electrical Engineering, Computer Science and Informatics (EECSI)
abstract: Bali is a tourist destination with the largest market share in Indonesia. So the progress of Bali tourism has a major contribution to the country's foreign exchange earnings. This of course cannot be separated from the support of the Bali hotel industry. This research intends to reveal the potential for hotel development in Bali based on sentiment analysis and analysis of tourist characteristics through data analytic processes. From the results of the sentiment analysis, several aspects were obtained that can be used as references to strengthen and maintain the positive image, such as the friendliness of the staff and improving aspects that cause tourist dissatisfaction, such as room replacement. So hotel services in Bali will get better. The potential for hotel improvement in Bali can also be supported by understanding the characteristics of the guests. This research uses a clustering method to group tourists who stay in star hotels and budget hotels. Understanding the characteristics of each tourist cluster can be a reference for marketing strategies and decision-making in this industry.

articleTitle: K-Means Clustering Analysis to Identify Electrical Load Consumption Patterns Based on Primary Energy Consumption
publicationTitle: 2024 11th International Conference on Electrical Engineering, Computer Science and Informatics (EECSI)
