abstract: Electricity consumption in Indonesia has experienced significant growth along with economic development and infrastructure expansion. However, the main challenge lies in managing energy efficiently to meet the growing demand. A deep understanding of electricity load consumption patterns is essential for effective energy management. The K-Means Clustering method is used in this study to cluster primary energy consumption data and electricity load consumption. This study aims to implement electricity load modeling by finding the closest data distribution distance, which is divided into 3 clusters. From the results of the implementation of the method, a value of 0.067820466 was obtained as the closest minimum value in cluster 1 of the untransposed system load data, 0.533624 as the minimum value distance in cluster 2 of the transposed system load data, and 0.067820466 as the minimum value distance in cluster 3 of the power plant data with a silhouette coefficient value indicating good and imperfect cluster quality in the data used.

articleTitle: Data Security in Intelligent System for Road Maintenance Using Encryption and HTTPS
publicationTitle: 2024 11th International Conference on Electrical Engineering, Computer Science and Informatics (EECSI)
abstract: A highly maintained toll road decreases accident risk, improves traffic efficiency, and enhances infrastructure feasibility, resulting in reduced maintenance costs. This study presents the implementation of data security in an intelligent toll road maintenance system using AES encryption and HTTPS protocols. The proposed system consists of NodeMCU ESP-12 as the microcontroller, MPU6050 accelerometer for measuring vehicle vibrations, Neo-6M GPS module for location tracking, and an SD card module for data storage. The collected data is encrypted using AES before being transmitted securely over HTTPS. Experimental results show that the system enhances data security with an encryption time of 1884 ms using AES+HTTP and 5721 ms using AES+HTTPS, demonstrating the feasibility of this approach despite the increased processing time.

articleTitle: Modified Genetic Algorithm for Capacitive Compensation in Radial Distribution Systems
publicationTitle: 2024 11th International Conference on Electrical Engineering, Computer Science and Informatics (EECSI)
abstract: This paper introduces an Modified Genetic Algorithm (MGA) for optimizing the placement of capacitor banks in radial distribution systems to minimize active power losses. In MGA, the crossover and mutation processes adapt based on each chromosome's fitness value. Chromosomes with high fitness values perform local searches to enhance efficiency, while those with low fitness values conduct global searches to prevent premature convergence. Additionally, an ‘OR’ operator is incorporated into the crossover process to improve the algorithm's performance. This operator ensures that offspring from high-fitness parents have higher or at least comparable fitness values to the best parent. M GA has been tested on 33-bus and 69-bus systems, demonstrating superior optimization results compared to other methods, as evidenced by the lowest power losses achieved.

articleTitle: Mooc Course Recommendation System Model with Explainable AI (XAI) Using Content Based Filtering Method
publicationTitle: 2024 11th International Conference on Electrical Engineering, Computer Science and Informatics (EECSI)
abstract: Massive Open Online Course (MOOC) is a type of online course that has been designed and can be accessed by all individuals via the internet. The problem that is often found in MOOCs is the lack of a recommendation system provided by the algorithm of the MOOC. This research is conducted to analyze a recommendation system that applies the Content Based Filtering approach in order to solve the problems that occur. The recommendation system analyzed will function as a media that provides recommendations to users based on their preferences. By utilizing content-based methods, the recommendations given are expected to be exactly what the user wants. The level of explainability of the recommendation system is further emphasized by XAI using ELI5. By getting a concise explanation when a recommendation is given, the system will gain more trust from users for providing an appropriate recommendation. The assessment of the accuracy of the recommendation system model is measured using MAE. By researching this recommendation system using XAI, it is hoped that it can help future systems to improve the quality of the course recommendation system.

articleTitle: Optimizing Energy Yield: A Comparative Study of North and East-Facing Vertical Bifacial Photovoltaic Modules in Indonesia
publicationTitle: 2024 11th International Conference on Electrical Engineering, Computer Science and Informatics (EECSI)
abstract: A bstract-Bifacial photovoltaic module is a photovoltaic technology that can absorb solar radiation from both sides of the module (front and rear) which aims to increase the efficiency of the photovoltaic module. In general, photovoltaic modules are installed at a tilt or horizontally, the disadvantages of which include the accumulation of dust and dirt on the surface of the photovoltaic module, less efficient use of space and higher maintenance requirements. In this paper, an evaluation of the power generation of bifacial photovoltaic modules installed vertically in tropical climates such as Indonesia was carried out. Where a comparison of the PV facing (azimuth direction) between those facing east and those facing north was carried out. The results of the study showed that the maximum power of bifacial photovoltaic facing north reached 224.8 W during the day, while those facing east had a maximum power generation of 201.4 W in the morning. Overall, the power generation of bifacial photovoltaic facing north was higher than that facing east with an average generation efficiency of 5.93 % and 4.58% respectively.

articleTitle: Development of a Data Generation System with Various Loading Conditions for Capacitor Placement and Sizing Studies
publicationTitle: 2024 11th International Conference on Electrical Engineering, Computer Science and Informatics (EECSI)
abstract: Power efficiency can be achieved in distribution systems by maintaining voltage stability and reducing transmission line losses. One of the solutions is through the installation of capacitor banks to compensate for the lagging power factor at the load. This installation improves the power factor. In improving the power factor, the volt-ampere demand is reduced, hence reducing current demand and thereby reducing line losses and voltage drops. The research on optimal capacitor placement and sizing is rich considering different techniques, from mathematical-based techniques to the recent application of artificial intelligence-based solutions. While previous research has yielded good results that have contributed to this area of power system efficiency, most optimal capacitor studies assume rated conditions or at steady-state conditions. While steady state conditions are acceptable, it does not provide an accurate representation of the state of the power system. There has been research where optimal capacitor placement and sizing studies have considered different loading conditions, however, some of these studies either employ capacitor switching, or use insufficient loading conditions without basis. This paper provides a basis for the development of power system loading conditions to aid for a more comprehensive solution methodology of optimal capacitor studies. It is based on the principle that the load demand of a power system can be simplified into discrete approximations that still provide accurate representation of the power demand in the power system through achieving the intended percent loading of the system with a negligible ± 0.00001 or ± 0.5% error.

articleTitle: Numerical Computation and Characterisation of Vivaldi Phased Array Antenna Applied for C-Band Radar
publicationTitle: 2024 11th International Conference on Electrical Engineering, Computer Science and Informatics (EECSI)
abstract: Conventional radar systems rely on mechanical components to rotate the antenna and direct the signal to reach the targeted moving obj ects such as airplane and helicopter, thereby limiting the scanning speed of the intended monitoring area. These mechanical components are prone to wear and damage, resulting in more frequent maintenance and potential system failures. Current research activity focuses on the use of phased array antenna which employs electronic control for area scanning and enable beamforming without the need for rotational movement of the physical radar antenna part. The design of an antipodal Vivaldi phased array antenna was constructed through the optimized numerical computation to capable of operating within the C-band radar applications. In this study, a single high-gain antenna was preliminary designed to obtain the total array configuration gain 14.2 dBi. Through phase control, the antenna can manipulate its radiation pattern up to 60°. Simulation results indicate a maximum return loss of -32.5 dB and a maximum bandwidth of 3,400 MHz (4.6 GHz - 8 GHz). Vivaldi phased array antenna is suitable for radar applications in the specified frequency range, providing efficient performance in terms of return loss, bandwidth, and beam steering capability. The designed phased array antenna can be utilized in ultra wide band (UWB) radar systems.

articleTitle: Simulation and Experimental Validation of a Piezoelectric Vibration Damping System for CubeSat
publicationTitle: 2024 11th International Conference on Electrical Engineering, Computer Science and Informatics (EECSI)
abstract: CubeSat missions much like other traditional satellites face the issue of experiencing intense vibration and shock during space travel. Within the scope of the onboard telemetry tracking and command system, vibration can result in latency which degrades the performance of the system. This paper presents a comprehensive study on piezoelectric shunt damping for CubeSats, focusing on both simulation and experimental validation. The piezoelectric shunt damping system prototype developed in this paper was able to achieve a shunted voltage of 5 mV, a displacement amplitude decrement of 40%, a damping ratio of 0.223 and an overall system latency of 24 ms. The effectiveness of the proposed piezoelectric shunt damping system prototype is evaluated in comparison to other referenced shunt damping systems.

articleTitle: Solving Non-Convex Economic Dispatch Problems using Symbiotic Organisms Search Algorithm
publicationTitle: 2024 11th International Conference on Electrical Engineering, Computer Science and Informatics (EECSI)
abstract: Energy is one of the living sectors of the economy. With the current needs of activities from entertainment to production and business, many types of energy have been born to serve the needs of society. The common characteristic of using these types of energy is the cost reduction while increasing energy supply efficiency. This article focuses on solving the optimal economic problem in using new energy sources. Use SOSA to analyze systems with 10 devices and 40 devices. To achieve effective results, this result is compared with the results solved by other algorithms. The results show that SOSA gives better solutions than other algorithms (0.01 % - 1.11%).

articleTitle: AI-Powered Chatbots in Health Insurance: Assessing Their Effectiveness in Consumer Search Processes
publicationTitle: 2024 11th International Conference on Electrical Engineering, Computer Science and Informatics (EECSI)
abstract: AI-powered chatbots are increasingly being adopted by the health insurance providers to improve customer service and streamline processes with the overarching goals of offering personalized assistance and handling complex tasks. However, due to limited research, the understanding of AI-powered chatbots' effectiveness in the health insurance search process remains limited. The aim of this study is to assess the effectiveness of AI-powered chatbots in the health insurance search process to traditional search methods based on consumer satisfaction, decision-making ability, and perceived risks. The study used a purposive sampling technique and a structured online questionnaire to collect data from 123 respondents who had health insurance and interacted with chatbots while searching a health insurance plan. The findings revealed that respondents were more satisfied with AI-powered chatbots for obtaining information and query resolution, but less satisfied with the information quality provided by AI-powered chatbots. According to the study, respondents perceived higher risks of data privacy, user security, and information accuracy when using AI-powered chatbots. The study thereby provides valuable insights for technology developers and health insurance providers.

articleTitle: Performance Assessment of Advanced CNN and Transformer Architectures in Skin Cancer Detection
publicationTitle: 2024 11th International Conference on Electrical Engineering, Computer Science and Informatics (EECSI)
abstract: Skin cancer has always been one of the most common types of cancer in medical history. Every year, it kills millions of people around the world. To find skin problems early, it is necessary to have a reliable automated method for recognizing them. In the past, protein sequences and different types of imaging methods were used with machine learning to find skin cancer. The problem with machine learning methods is that they need features to be designed by humans, which is hard to do and takes a lot of time. Image processing and deep learning are both used in the method for treating skin cancer that works. Our study is based on The HAM10000 dataset, which is made up of 10015 different dermatoscopic pictures of common pigmented skin lesions from different sources. The newest deep learning techniques, such as Convolutional Neural Networks (CNN), Transformers, and Hybrid models, i.e., ConvNeXt V2, Swinv2, ViT2, Cvt, DenseNet, RestNet, PVTv2, EfficientNet, EfficientFormer, VGG, MobileNet, MobileViTV2, GoogLeNet, are all compared in this study to see which one is better for automatically detecting skin cancer lesions. We found the best model for identifying skin lesions by determining its accuracy, F1-score, Inference time, and confusion matrix. Among our implemented models, the ConvNeXt V2 model has an accuracy of 93.2 % with the lowest inference time. With this research's help, new ways are being made to find skin cancer, which can lead to better patient results and better clinical decisions.

articleTitle: EfficientNet-Based Approach for Enhanced Sugarcane Disease Classification: Implementation and Evaluation
publicationTitle: 2024 11th International Conference on Electrical Engineering, Computer Science and Informatics (EECSI)
abstract: Classifying plant diseases is essential for maintaining crop health and agricultural productivity. Technological advancements have shifted plant disease classification from traditional manual inspections to automated, precise techniques. This evolution is crucial for sugarcane, a vital crop impacting numerous economies. Deep learning techniques have yet to be applied to classify sugarcane plant diseases. Early methods relied on handcrafted features and basic algorithms, but sophisticated machine learning and deep learning techniques have revolutionized this field. Deep learning models such as Inception, ResNet, DenseNet, and MobileNet, trained on large datasets, have been instrumental in plant disease classification. With its compound scaling method, EfficientNet achieves superior accuracy while maintaining computational efficiency, outperforming other models in generalization and classification accuracy. Standard datasets like Plant Village and Leaf Snap have become benchmarks, but no comprehensive dataset has existed for sugarcane diseases until now. This research introduces the sugarcane disease dataset, implementing the EfficientNet model for classification that has reached 92.50%, 96,81%, and 91,26% in test and validation accuracy also mobileNetV3 Large reach 98,86 for validation accuracy on augmented sugarcane dataset. We compare these models with other established methods, demonstrating EfficientNet's superior performance through detailed visualizations of confusion matrix and accuracy graphs, which significantly contribute to sugarcane disease management.

articleTitle: Effectiveness of Various Smoothing Filters on Malaria Cell Image Quality
publicationTitle: 2024 11th International Conference on Electrical Engineering, Computer Science and Informatics (EECSI)
abstract: Malaria is one of the most vulnerable diseases attacking human health, with rising cases from year to year. Therefore, technological developments are required to overcome this disease. Currently, the examination of malaria is carried out by examining human blood using a microscope, and the results are diagnosed using artificial intelligence (AI) technology. To improve the diagnosis results, this research compared the effectiveness of three image smoothing methods (average, Gaussian, and median filters) in reducing Gaussian and Salt and Pepper noise, commonly present in malaria cell images. These filters were tested on four different noise levels and analyzed based on PSNR, SNR, MSE, and SSIM values to determine the most effective filter. The results unveiled that the average filter depicted the most remarkable performance on Gaussian noise, while the median filter produced the highest outcome on Salt and Pepper noise.

articleTitle: Hate Speech Classification Using Mixed Language Feature Modification and Machine Learning Approach
publicationTitle: 2024 11th International Conference on Electrical Engineering, Computer Science and Informatics (EECSI)
abstract: Hate speech is often considered vague or contradictory in its definitions, generally referring to various kinds of negative expressions by users, including insults and harsh criticism. To clarify, it is suggested to focus on references to violence in a statement and discriminatory content. Things like negative stereotypes, expressions of violence, dehumanization, hurting or killing, and insults that use offensive language, slurs, denigrating with metaphors, and wordplays. This study investigates the effectiveness of different machine learning and deep learning models for hate speech classification, evaluating the impact of stopword removal preprocessing and feature expansion techniques (FastText and Word2Vec). Our findings indicate that not performing stopword removal can slightly improve accuracy compared to preprocessing with stopword removal. Furthermore, feature expansion had minimal impact on classification accuracy. Among the models tested, BERT-Large achieved the highest accuracy of 85.16%, significantly outperforming traditional machine learning models (Linear Support Vector Classifier (SVC), SVC, Random Forest) and other deep learning models (Long Short-Term Memory (LSTM), Convolutional Neural Network (CNN)). These results suggest that transformer-based models like Bidirectional Encoder Representation of Transformers (BERT) are particularly effective for hate speech classification, while feature expansion techniques may not be crucial for enhancing model performance.

articleTitle: Identification of the Role of Universities in Sustainable Development Goals (SDGs) Based on GARUDA Indexed Publications Using BERT
publicationTitle: 2024 11th International Conference on Electrical Engineering, Computer Science and Informatics (EECSI)
abstract: Sustainable Development Goals (SDGs) are a global commitment agreed upon by all Member States of the United Nations (UN) as the 2030 agenda, to realize a better and more sustainable world life. Indonesia, which is one of the UN member countries, must also commit to realizing the achievement of the 17 goals in the SDGs. Universities have an important role in achieving the SDGs goals, research aims to achieve this by identifying the track record of research and scientific publications that have been carried out by universities. GARUDA (Garba Rujukan Digital) is the official repository portal of the Indonesian government that provides access to various sources of scientific knowledge, including journals and proceedings published by universities in Indonesia. To find out the extent of the role of universities, it can be done by identifying the SDGs category of scientific publications conducted by researchers and indexed by GARUDA. This study aims to develop an SDGs category identification system using the DistilBERT model which is a distillation version of BERT. From the testing conducted on the testing data from GARUDA, the results of accuracy, precision, recall, and f1-score were obtained at 0.82. These results indicate that the model has quite good performance in identifying SDGs categories based on abstract data from GARUDA-indexed scientific publications written by university researchers in Indonesia.

articleTitle: Multi-Layer Hiding Scheme for Image Data Using Crypto-Stego with Compression Technique
publicationTitle: 2024 11th International Conference on Electrical Engineering, Computer Science and Informatics (EECSI)
abstract: In this modern era, the size of image data grows significantly due to increasing data needs. However, as the data flows become faster, data security concerns should receive more attention. This paper proposes a Crypto-Stego technique to enhance image data security and reduce data size using compression technique. The size of image data is reduced using Discrete Wavelet Transform (DWT) compression. Then, the compressed secret image will be encrypted with Advanced Encryption Standard using Cipher Block Chaining (AES-CBC). Lastly, the Least Significant Bit technique is used to embed the encrypted secret image inside the cover image. The results are illustrated by numerous testing simulation achieving an average score 37.9dB in the PSNR metric and 0.96 in SSIM metric.

articleTitle: An Analysis of Electrical Energy Usage in Social Consumers Using Fuzzy C Means
publicationTitle: 2024 11th International Conference on Electrical Engineering, Computer Science and Informatics (EECSI)
abstract: The objective of this study is to examine the patterns of electrical energy usage in social consumers by employing the Fuzzy C Means clustering method to assist utility companies in the development of business strategies, operations, planning, and energy policies that are customized to the specific needs of each group. The problem of unpredictable social activities, changes in work patterns, and community activities, particularly among social consumers, result in significant declines and irregular electricity consumption patterns. It is crucial for energy providers to comprehend these evolving patterns to effectively manage electricity supplies. This research was carried out in a 5-step process, namely Data Collection, Data Preprocessing, Clustering Process with Fuzzy C Means (FCM), find pattern and clustering validity. This study sources its data from the Automatic Meter Reading (AMR) of social consumers, specifically places of worship, educational institutions, and health services. We employ the Fuzzy C Means (FCM) Clustering method to categorize electrical energy consumption patterns into multiple groups, considering similarities in the data. The variables utilized in this analysis are kilowatt (kW) and kilovolt-ampere (kVA). The findings indicate that places of worship, educational institutions, and health services exhibit distinct patterns of electrical energy usage, although belonging to the same electricity tariff category. The quality of cluster results in this research using the Davies-Bouldin index (DBI) method is 0.51, which shows that the resulting clustering has a fairly good level of separation and compactness.

articleTitle: Scenarios to Handle Shifts Data Pattern Using Neural Network for Forecasting Indonesian GDP Based on Financial Growth at Risk
publicationTitle: 2024 11th International Conference on Electrical Engineering, Computer Science and Informatics (EECSI)
abstract: Modeling time series data through statistical techniques is a common practice in economics, primarily aimed at forecasting economic indicators such as GDP to prepare for future trends. Over time, statistical modeling has increasingly incorporated machine learning (ML) methods. Although ML offers flexibility in model equations, accurate projections still require that future data patterns align with historical ones, which is often not the case. This research examines the impact of changes or shifts in time series data patterns by exploring various scenarios for determining the length of training data used in modeling. As an empirical application, this study also provides a framework for projecting Indonesia's GDP by utilizing financial indicators such as the Financial Stress Index (FSI) as predictors. The model employed is QRNN-MIDAS, which accommodates differences in the frequency of responses variable (quarterly) and predictors (monthly) to estimate high-frequency financial Growth-at-Risk (GaR)-based on GDP growth, ultimately applied to forecast the actual GDP value. The analysis identifies the optimal scenario as one using a year-on-year GDP growth calculation with data limited to the period following a shift in the data pattern (from 2011 to 2023) and including a dummy predictor variable for the COVID-19 pandemic. According to this scenario, Indonesia's economic growth in 2024 is projected to be between 3.64% and 6%, with the GDP at constant 2010 prices ranging from 2.96 to 3.13 trillion rupiah. Assuming no unforeseen adverse events, Indonesia's economy in 2024 is expected to be stable and show a tendency to grow.

articleTitle: Outbound Logistic Critical Process Improvement Planning Based on Business Process Evaluation: a Case Study in the Bicycle Industry
publicationTitle: 2024 11th International Conference on Electrical Engineering, Computer Science and Informatics (EECSI)
abstract: The supply chain team of a bicycle company wants to evaluate the current outbound logistics operations, which are motivated by attaining lean logistics and reducing truck wait time. As a result, an entire outbound logistics business process is established using the company's standard framework, known as the Responsible, Accountable, Consulted, and Informed (RACI) Matrix. Waste analysis shows that 58% of stuffing activity is nonvalue added. It entails Empty containers which are waiting to be filled and bringing the prepared goods back to the loading dock operations. The distribution of operators and open containers, as well as the loading dock's overcapacity, are the root causes of waste. A propose improvement regarding resource optimization and the number of containers was made using the ProModel. The result of the first proposed model will increase the stuffing speed to 0.51 containers/hour and increase operator utility by 24.055%. The second suggestion is to design the staging bin as temporary storage.

articleTitle: Client Risk Assessment in a Network: An Examination of Man-in-the-Middle Attacks and Their Usage
publicationTitle: 2024 11th International Conference on Electrical Engineering, Computer Science and Informatics (EECSI)
abstract: This research investigates the impact of Man-In-The-Middle (MITM) attacks on network environments, mainly clients, due to a lack of advanced security measures. The study uses a Kali Linux network and a ticketing application to test data traffic and examine DNS spoofing, where the attacker alters the client's IP address and MAC address to the attacker's, disrupting data exchanges between the client and server. The findings highlight the ease with which hackers can monitor traffic and intercept data packets during client-server communication. The study also emphasizes the need for robust security protocols, especially with the increasing adoption of IoT devices. VLANs are necessary to protect these devices from potential attacks. Continuous improvement and innovation in cybersecurity measures are crucial for staying ahead of evolving threats. Implementing SSL services, using VPNs and HTTPS protocols, and maintaining up-to-date security patches and malware updates are essential for protecting network environments.

articleTitle: A Heart Sound Identification System Built on Android-Based Electronic Stethoscope for Healthcare Development
publicationTitle: 2024 11th International Conference on Electrical Engineering, Computer Science and Informatics (EECSI)
abstract: Heart disease is a significant cause of death worldwide and the highest cause of death in Indonesia. With over 7000 islands, the geography of Indonesia presents substantial challenges in managing heart disease, particularly in remote and underdeveloped areas. Early detection is crucial in reducing mortality rates associated with heart disease. However, this process can be expensive and relies heavily on clinicians for accurate detection. Technological advancements have led to smartphones with increasingly sophisticated capabilities, supporting the development of mobile health applications for remote health monitoring. This study aims to develop an electronic stethoscope with a total hardware cost under a hundred rupiah that connects to an Android-based smartphone application for heart sound signal identification. The application provides a reliable validation method that reduces reliance on clinicians. Heart sound signal processing uses the fifth level of the Discrete Wavelet Transform method for noise reduction, using Daubechies 4 as the mother wavelet and the Linear Envelope method for heart sound identification. The instrument design incorporates a cost-effective stethoscope, setting it apart from other electronic stethoscopes on the market. The heart sound identification method was tested on 20 individuals, and it was found that the recorded heart signal data generated accurate identification results in 95.67% of total heart cycles.

articleTitle: Preprocessing with Skin Segmentation to Improve Monk Skin Tone (MST) Classification
publicationTitle: 2024 11th International Conference on Electrical Engineering, Computer Science and Informatics (EECSI)
abstract: Skin tones come in a diverse range of shades and are often necessary for various computer vision tasks. While skin detection is a well-studied focus, skin tone classification is not. Most works also use the Fitzpatrick Skin Type (FST) scale despite it being developed for skin phototype classification purposes. Due to the lack of a proper skin tone scale, the Monk Skin Tone (MST) was created, which was used to perform skin tone classification using Convolutional Neural Network (CNN) model as well as the Individual Topology Angle (ITA) value threshold method with skin segmentation as a preprocessing for both classification methods. To investigate if skin segmentation can improve classification accuracy, the MST classification was performed using both segmented and unsegmented images involving the IT A value threshold method as well as two CNN models that were trained using different image types. The experimental results showed that the best way to perform MST classification was using a CNN model trained and tested with segmented images, which yielded the highest accuracy score being 0.91, with no signs of over or underfitting. The results also supported that segmentation is necessary, and that it can improve a classification model's accuracy.

articleTitle: Enhancing Tangible Cultural Heritage Preservation through Virtual Reality: A Case Study of Watu Gong Sites in Indonesia
publicationTitle: 2024 11th International Conference on Electrical Engineering, Computer Science and Informatics (EECSI)
abstract: This research addresses the intersection of cultural heritage preservation and modern digital technologies, focusing on the application of Virtual Reality (VR) to enhance the accessibility and engagement of cultural heritage sites. Using Indonesia's Watugong Sites as a case study, this study explores developing and implementing a VR application designed to provide an immersive and interactive experience of cultural heritage sites. The study's methodology using a design thinking approach, involved the design, development, and user evaluation of a VR application tailored for the Watugong Sites. According to the findings, a significant majority of respondents expressed complete satisfaction with the VR experience, particularly highlighting its effectiveness in enhancing the attractiveness of the cultural sites. It suggests a promising future for integrating VR in cultural heritage preservation, highlighting its capacity to enhance public engagement and education, and ultimately contribute to the sustainability of tourism and heritage conservation efforts.

articleTitle: Multi-Modal Tracking Using LiDAR and Visual Signals
publicationTitle: 2024 11th International Conference on Electrical Engineering, Computer Science and Informatics (EECSI)
abstract: Multi-object tracking (MOT) is a crucial technique for detecting and tracking multiple objects over time in a scene. It involves locating objects in consecutive frames of a video or sequential observations and establishing correspondences to maintain their identity. MOT is essential in various applications, including autonomous vehicles, robotics, and video surveillance. In autonomous vehicles, it is typically performed using 3D models (LiDAR/stereo) or 2D models (one or more RGB cameras). The LiDAR 3D point-cloud provides a 360-degree view of its surroundings but has a low resolution compared to the camera's visual signals. This paper presents a sensor fusion approach for multi-object detection and tracking, combining object detection information from sensors, LiDAR, and cameras and applying data association algorithms like Hungarian algorithms for tracking to increase the overall system. The EagerMOT approach for 3D Multi-Object Tracking via Sensor Fusion achieves state-of-the-art results across several MOT tasks on the KITTI dataset, achieving an accuracy of 87.95 %.

articleTitle: Leveraging Artificial Intelligence and Internet of Things for Advanced Disaster Drone Technology
publicationTitle: 2024 11th International Conference on Electrical Engineering, Computer Science and Informatics (EECSI)
abstract: Disaster management involves critical decisions where precision and accuracy are vital. Our research focuses on using artificial intelligence (AI) and Internet-of-the-Things (IoT) based drones to enhance situational awareness in disaster-stricken areas. These drones, powered by advanced deep learning algorithms, provide real-time aerial imagery, detect signs of life under rubble, and operate effectively in adverse weather conditions, including heavy rain and flooding. Equipped with gas sensors, they ensure the safety of both rescuers and survivors by detecting harmful gases. Additionally, the drones facilitate communication with survivors and support coordination during rescue operations. Using COCO, Fire datasets, and the YOLO model, our method achieved results with a fire detection precision of 97.5 %, recall of 92.3%, and an Fl-score of 95.5%. This innovative approach aims to revolutionize disaster response by making operations more effective and safer for everyone involved.

articleTitle: Development of Interactive Websites to Promote Road Safety Awareness Among Primary School Children - LINTAS
publicationTitle: 2024 11th International Conference on Electrical Engineering, Computer Science and Informatics (EECSI)

authors.preferredName: Wan Nur Idayu Tun Mohd Hassan

abstract: Road safety education is essential for primary school children to reduce traffic-related injuries and fatalities. The Road Safety Department (JKJR) and the Malaysian Institute of Road Safety Research (MIROS) have developed a Road Safety Education (RSE) Module integrated into the Bahasa Melayu curriculum. This study focuses on designing and developing interactive websites that promote road safety awareness among primary school students. Through the use of interactive website, the study aims to create an engaging educational tool that captivates and informs young learners. Traditional methods, such as physical books, present challenges in maintaining students' interest. Moreover, there is a significant lack of interactive road safety education websites, particularly tailored to the needs of primary school students, like Pendidikan Keselamatan Jalan Raya (PKJR). This scarcity extends to the limited availability of game-based learning platforms for road safety education. The study addresses this gap by developing LINTAS, an initiative that offers a comprehensive set of educational tools, including flashcards and an interactive website, to engage children effectively. These resources aim to equip students with the knowledge to recognize road hazards, avoid accidents, and practice safe pedestrian behavior. By fostering an understanding of road safety through engaging digital tools, the project seeks to safeguard children's well-being during their daily commutes and everyday activities. Ultimately, the use of digital platforms in education encourages active learning, enhances academic performance, and instills a lasting awareness of road safety.

articleTitle: Parallel Hybrid 2D Convolutional Neural Networks and Recurrent Neural Networks in EEG Post-Stroke Identification Based on EEG Signal
publicationTitle: 2024 11th International Conference on Electrical Engineering, Computer Science and Informatics (EECSI)
abstract: Electroencephalogram (EEG) captures brain activity that can used for diagnosis and monitoring stroke scale. EEG signals contain spatial and temporal information to analyze signals with stroke characteristics. This research proposed a parallel hybrid approach using 2D Convolutional Neural Networks (2D CNN) and Recurrent Neural Networks. The Wavelet method obtains Delta, Theta, and Alpha wave representations of the EEG signals, representing the characteristic post-stroke frequencies (1 – 13 Hz). This approach, in parallel, uses 2D CNN for spatial feature extraction from each waveform, while RNN-GRU is used for temporal analysis within each signal segment. Experiments were conducted using an EEG dataset from 75 subjects, evaluating five techniques for weight correction. The results show that the parallel hybrid 2D CNN-GRU model achieves an 89.96-90.96% accuracy. However, the weight correction technique and learning rate influence performance but are insignificant. The SGD optimizer with a learning rate of 0.01 achieved the highest accuracy, although it required a longer training time.

articleTitle: Automated Monitoring of Oocytes During the Extracorporeal Maturation Process
publicationTitle: 2024 11th International Conference on Electrical Engineering, Computer Science and Informatics (EECSI)
abstract: Efficient and accurate oocyte monitoring is crucial for ensuring their quality during maturation. Manual observation often disrupts the oocyte maturation process, potentially affecting oocyte quality. To address this issue, we propose a method for automated monitoring of oocytes during the maturation process. Our method employs the Tenengrad algorithm for initial well edge focusing, followed by spiral scanning and the Circle Hough Transform for oocyte detection. Detected oocytes are centered in the camera frame, and fine focusing is achieved using the Tenengrad method. Experimental results show that our approach reduces monitoring time while maintaining consistent oocyte po-sitioning, with the initial search time of 50.63 seconds decreasing to an average of 21.3 seconds for subsequent searches and an average deviation in oocyte positioning of approximately 21.62 µm, indicating high accuracy. This demonstrates the efficiency and reliability of our automated monitoring method, providing a robust solution for real-time oocyte monitoring without manual intervention.

articleTitle: Optimizing Battery Consumption for Android-based Automatic Identification System (AIS) Application for Indonesian Fishermen
publicationTitle: 2024 11th International Conference on Electrical Engineering, Computer Science and Informatics (EECSI)
abstract: Fishing is integral to Indonesia's economy and the livelihood of many citizens. Indonesian fishermen often spend long periods at sea with limited access to power, making energy efficiency crucial for mobile applications, especially those used for navigation and safety. AIS is vital for maritime navigation, providing real-time information on vessel locations, weather, and emergencies. However, high battery consumption can cause AIS apps to fail when needed most. This study aims to optimize battery consumption for a mobile app used by Indonesian fishermen by implementing techniques like batch data transmission, efficient background task management, and optimized location services. The effectiveness of these techniques was evaluated based on key performance indicators such as battery usage, latency, data transmission, and task completion rates. The results show a significant reduction in average battery usage from 3000 mAh to 2000 mAh and improved application performance with latency decreasing from 150 ms to 120 ms. Data transmission reduced by 10% and task completion rates increased from 85% to 95%. Further analysis revealed that Wi-Fi networks are more energy-efficient than cellular networks, with average battery usage of 1800 mAh compared to 2200 mAh. Enhancing the energy efficiency of mobile applications is crucial for users in remote areas with limited power resources. The implemented techniques improved the reliability and efficiency of the AIS application, thereby enhancing the safety and operational effectiveness of Indonesian fishermen at sea.

articleTitle: Analyzing User Engagement in a Fraction Learning App for Elementary Students
publicationTitle: 2024 11th International Conference on Electrical Engineering, Computer Science and Informatics (EECSI)
abstract: Fractions are a crucial part of mathematics education, but their abstract nature and complex operations often pose significant challenges for elementary students, potentially leading to future academic difficulties. To address this issue, a study was conducted to develop and implement a Fraction Learning App to enhance fraction understanding among elementary students. Initial results indicated that students using the app significantly outperformed traditional methods, showing higher engagement and improved learning outcomes. Despite these positive results, there is a need to delve deeper into user behavior to optimize the app's effectiveness. Understanding which features and sub-features are most and least used and analyzing daily and hourly usage patterns can provide valuable insights. Additionally, segmenting users based on engagement levels can inform targeted interventions. This study addressed three key research questions: the usage patterns of app features, daily and hourly usage trends, and user engagement levels. Findings revealed that specific features were more engaging, usage peaked during certain times, and distinct user segments exhibited different engagement characteristics. These insights are critical for refining the app, ensuring it meets diverse student needs, and enhancing educational outcomes. Future research should explore long-term impacts, scalability, and additional technological integrations to improve learning experiences further.

articleTitle: Multi-Output DC Power Supply Using Push-Pull Converter Powered from PV Modules
publicationTitle: 2024 11th International Conference on Electrical Engineering, Computer Science and Informatics (EECSI)
abstract: This paper presents designing and making a multi-output DC power supply (MOPS) feeding from the PV modules. The MOPS is based on a push-pull converter topology that provides four output channels of 12-V 1-A each and will be used to supply the control circuit of the six-step power inverter that drives the 3-phase squirrel cage induction motor of the centrifugal pump. This MOPS, along with the inverter, the induction motor, and other circuits, are the main parts that construct the battery-less solar water pumping system. The push-pull converter is controlled by the PWM controller SG3525 and operated as an open-loop controller with switching frequency of 20 kHz. Since it works without a feedback element, the linear voltage regulator LM7812 has been placed on each output channel of the push-pull converter to obtain regulated 12-V voltage. The functional test was conducted on the MOPS, and the result showed that the power supply could maintain regulated voltage at each output channel from no-load to 100-ohm load conditions.

articleTitle: Sentiment Analysis of Thesis Policy by Instagram Users Using Logistic Regression
publicationTitle: 2024 11th International Conference on Electrical Engineering, Computer Science and Informatics (EECSI)
abstract: The requirements for university graduation were changed by the Minister of Education, Culture, Research and Technology in August 2023, where a thesis is no longer required and can be replaced with another form. The existence of this regulation has caused discussion in the community with various responses visible through social media Instagram. Instagram has become a forum for sharing the latest topics for the public, causing the emergence of online media accounts such as Folkative. This research aims to analyze sentiment regarding the policy of eliminating thesis obligations at universities through data collected from comments on Folkative's Instagram account posts. Sentiment analysis was carried out using Logistic Regression for classification, K-Fold Cross Validation for data validation, Confusion Matrix for evaluation, and ADASYN to resolve data imbalances. The data collected from the scraping process was 4,172 comments. After carrying out the classification and performance evaluation process, the best method produced was a combination of Logistic Regression and ADASYN achieving results of 89.6% accuracy, 91.5% precision, 87.7% recall, and f-1 score 89.5%. This shows that the performance of the Logistic Regression method is good and suitable for use as a classification model in this research.

articleTitle: Cadastral: Blockchain-Based Land Registration System
publicationTitle: 2024 11th International Conference on Electrical Engineering, Computer Science and Informatics (EECSI)
abstract: In an era of evolving property management and ownership practices, blockchain technology emerges as a transformative force and revolutionizes traditional land registration systems. This conceptual approach is a vision of a future world where property transactions occur without glitches. Based on a network of nodes that perform the data distribution, blockchain does not require a central authority (decentralized) and significantly decreases the possibility of data manipulation. Utilizing blockchain's chain of custody and cryptographic features, a land registration system is strongly anticipated to counter existing challenges in the real estate industry, such as fraud, conflicts, and procedural bottlenecks that have been frustrating the industry for decades. The project deploys Solidity-based self-executing smart contracts to automate and enforce agreements related to property transfer, boosting efficiency and cutting out intermediaries. Users self-register and upload the required documents to the system. The critical aspect is that the user is verified only after the inspector meticulously assesses their details using the government database. After assessment, the user can use the application to sell or buy land. The inspector also surveys the land physically before granting permission to make the land available for purchase. The buyer and seller agree on a price before generating the ownership deed. Smart contracts are created for each of these steps from user registration to transfer of ownership, and stored in the local blockchain. Cryptographic algorithm, Hash Algorithm SHA-256 is utilized to protect user's sensitive information and keep anyone from unauthorized access and InterPlanetary File System (IPFS) for file storage.

articleTitle: Performance Enhancement of Electric Power Steering: A Review
publicationTitle: 2024 11th International Conference on Electrical Engineering, Computer Science and Informatics (EECSI)
abstract: In a few years, electric power steering technology has succeeded in replacing the hydraulic steering system and the electric hydraulic steering system. This technology has improved even more because electric vehicles have begun to be used. The study discusses issues related to improving electric power steering performance and provides an overview of the control strategies that have been implemented. The fist, the paper comprehensively introduces the classification of electric power steering and power assist. The second, application of control systems is presented, starting from conventional control including proportional-integral-derivative, continuing with artificial intelligence such as fuzzy logic control, artificial neural networks, to optimization using particle swarm optimization. Also discussed was identifying future challenges and opportunities.

articleTitle: Deep Sequence Models for Time Series Data: A Comparative Study and Parameter Fine-Tuning Approach
publicationTitle: 2024 11th International Conference on Electrical Engineering, Computer Science and Informatics (EECSI)
abstract: The modeling and prediction of time series data have become pivotal in data science and machine learning. Deep learning architectures, particularly Long Short-Term Memory (LSTM) networks, have proven effective in capturing complex temporal relationships, outperforming traditional methods. This study compares the performance of three LSTM variants-Convolutional LSTM (ConvLSTM), Bidirectional LSTM (BiLSTM), and Stacked LSTM-using datasets such as ETTh, ETTm, Energy, AQI, and Exchange Rate. Each model is trained and tested on subsets of these datasets, with hyperparameters like the number of layers, neurons, learning rate, batch size, optimizer, and loss function fine-tuned for optimal performance. The models are evaluated using metrics like Mean Squared Error (MSE), Root Mean Squared Error (RMSE), and Mean Absolute Error (MAE). Results indicate that ConvLSTM excels with spatiotemporal datasets, BiLSTM effectively captures full sequence contexts, and Stacked LSTM benefits from more in-depth representation. This research enhances the understanding of LSTM variants in time series analysis, demonstrating that fine-tuning can significantly boost performance. The findings apply to improving accuracy in time series forecasting across various fields.

articleTitle: Local Binary Pattern and Principal Component Analysis for Low-light Face Recognition
publicationTitle: 2024 11th International Conference on Electrical Engineering, Computer Science and Informatics (EECSI)
abstract: Facial recognition technology allows both the government and the general public to identify individuals based on their facial features, even in cases of significant changes. However, low lighting during the facial recognition process can lead to confusion during feature extraction, thus affecting facial recognition performance. This research aims to identify the most effective method for recognizing faces in low-light conditions. The Local Binary Pattern (LBP) and Principal Component Analysis (PCA) algorithms each have their strengths in feature extraction. These algorithms will be combined with others, including Histogram of Oriented Gradient (HOG), K-Nearest Neighbor (KNN), and Support Vector Machine (SVM). The process begins with face detection, followed by feature extraction using LBP, PCA, and HOG. Subsequently, these features will be classified using KNN and SVM. The combinations of these algorithms tested in this research include LBP-KNN, LBP-HOG-PCA-SVM, HOG-PCA-SVM, and MobileNet for additional comparison. The results indicate that the HOG-PCA-SVM combination achieved the highest accuracy among the other combinations, reaching 98%. This makes the HOG-PCA-SVM combination a preferred choice for low-light face recognition systems without image enhancement.

articleTitle: Noncontact Electrocardiogram System for Mattresses Using Silver Conductive Fabric
publicationTitle: 2024 11th International Conference on Electrical Engineering, Computer Science and Informatics (EECSI)
abstract: Electrocardiography (ECG) is an essential diagnostic tool in healthcare and widely used for monitoring heart activity. However, conventional wet electrodes, which rely on hydrogels containing nickel particles and acrylic adhesives, often cause discomfort and skin irritation during prolonged use. These drawbacks are particularly concerning for long-term ECG monitoring, which is crucial for detecting variations in heart rhythm that may not be obvious in shorter recordings. To overcome these challenges, this study explores a noncontact ECG measuring approach using silver fabric conductive dry electrodes. These dry electrodes were strategically placed under the shoulder blades, waist, and pelvis to effectively capture ECG signals. Given that raw ECG signals are inherently weak, they were amplified using an AD620 instrumentation amplifier, which offers a high common mode rejection ratio (CMRR) and differential gain, effectively reducing noise. The following amplification, the signals were subjected to filtering and baseline adjustment to ensure compatibility with microcontroller processing. The ECG signals were then processed using a 3rd level Discrete Wavelet Transform (DWT) to detect QRS complexes, which were used to calculate the heart rate and compare it with PPG sensor readings. Results indicated that the system performed best in the supine and right lateral positions, with error rates of 3.15% and 1.47%, respectively. This research demonstrated that silver fabric-conductive dry electrodes offer a more comfortable and less irritating solution for long-term cardiac monitoring.

articleTitle: Machine Learning Quantification of Liberica Coffee Morphology in Lipa City
publicationTitle: 2024 11th International Conference on Electrical Engineering, Computer Science and Informatics (EECSI)
abstract: Investigating the morphological characteristics of Liberica green coffee beans presents challenges due to their irregular shapes and potential overlaps within images. This study aimed to develop a robust image analysis pipeline for quantifying green bean morphology and exploring potential variations between farms within the Lipa City region. A comprehensive coffee bean collection protocol was established, and a diverse image dataset was created. Image preprocessing, including normalization, augmentation, and enhancement techniques, optimized the data for analysis. A U-Net convolutional neural network was developed for semantic segmentation, achieving remarkable performance with an accuracy of 99.83% and an IoU score of 0.985. This enabled the precise extraction of morphological features from individual bean instances. Principal Component Analysis (PCA) revealed the primary contributors to morphological variance, and Multivariate Analysis of Variance (MANDVA) demonstrated statistically significant differences in the overall combination of morphological features between farms. These findings suggest that farm origin, potentially due to variations in environmental conditions, cultivation practices, or bean varieties, influences the physical characteristics of Liberica green coffee beans. This study provides a powerful framework for future investigations into the relationship between morphology, quality assessment, and optimization of processing techniques within the coffee industry.

articleTitle: Exploring the Effectiveness and Efficiency of Electronic Testing Methods in Iraqi Higher Education Institutions: An Empirical Investigation
publicationTitle: 2024 11th International Conference on Electrical Engineering, Computer Science and Informatics (EECSI)
abstract: In Iraqi institutions, online education has emerged as an innovative way to conduct examinations and assessments in the wake of the COVID-19 outbreak. The purpose of this study is to gain a deeper understanding of the wider connotations of online evaluation techniques by examining the implementation of digital exams at a technical establishment in Iraq. For the purpose of evaluating their reactions to digital exams, two groups of 532 educators and 5,268 students were analyzed using descriptive statistics and inferential analysis. It appears that a large percentage of teachers (84%) and students (68%) believe the online exams fail to recognize top performers, which results in incorrect results. The online examination system was also viewed favorably by only 20 percent of educators and only 60 percent of pupils. According to the Lakeland Triple Rank Test, both sets of groups provided feedback within the mid-weight range of 1.76-2.54, indicating less disparity and more uniformity among educators. To boost evaluation reliability, a blend of traditional and digital learning methods was suggested to address the widespread dissatisfaction with digital examinations in technical education. For Iraq's technical instruction to be effective and trustworthy, robust infrastructure and extended training are necessary.

articleTitle: An Intrusion Detection System of Rough Set Theory Classification: Kyoto 2006+ Dataset
publicationTitle: 2024 11th International Conference on Electrical Engineering, Computer Science and Informatics (EECSI)
abstract: As telecommunication and information networks, which connect modern society through computers, smartphones, and other electronic devices, grow, so do security issues and cybercrime. The seriousness of cyberattacks in the context of network security has been highlighted by this rise in cybercrime. Simultaneously, machine learning has been thoroughly investigated for intrusion classification, with an emphasis on improving the accuracy of classifiers and the effectiveness of data mining models. This paper investigates the derivation of intrusion attack classification rules with Rough Set Theory (RST), a rule-based decision-making approach. To determine the efficacy of four different algorithms, including the Genetic Algorithm, experiments were carried out utilizing datasets that were made publicly available. When the Genetic Algorithm was used for rule construction in RST classification, the results were the best when compared to other rule generating techniques. Furthermore, this approach's capacity to precisely forecast all forms of attacks was shown when it was applied to a dataset of intrusion attacks that was made available to the public. Additionally, this methodology gives security professionals and developers useful information ahead of time, allowing them to take proactive measures when needed.

articleTitle: Suspect Identification Based on Facial Recognition from CCTV Using Hybrid Bat Algorithm
publicationTitle: 2024 11th International Conference on Electrical Engineering, Computer Science and Informatics (EECSI)
abstract: The incidence of criminal activity is rising steadily, necessitating the use of surveillance cameras to monitor and control such activities effectively. However, traditional video evaluation by human guards and manual image processing often fails to accurately analyze footage, especially when individuals use disguises like glasses, masks, hats, or different hairstyles. To address this issue, this research proposes a surveillance system that leverages CCTV footage to detect and identify individuals attempting to conceal their identities. The system first detects facial areas using the Multi-task Cascaded Convolutional Networks (MTCNN) method. Once a facial area is detected, the system performs face identification by matching facial features of suspects with those captured on CCTV. If a match of 70% or higher is found, the individual is flagged as a suspect, with the output showing bounding boxes around the face labeled with their name. To enhance the system's efficiency, the FaceNet embedding model is integrated with the Hybrid Bat Algorithm (HBA) to reduce the dimensionality of face embeddings. HBA, which combines modifications from the Bat Algorithm (BA) with Differential Evolution (DE) techniques, effectively optimizes the process. Evaluation results showed the best performance with a maximum iteration of 50 and a population size of 30, achieving an accuracy of 0.877, recall of 0.830, precision of 0.907, and f1-score of 0.867. The face embedding dimension was reduced from 512 to 201 using HBA.

articleTitle: A Text Mining Analysis of Social Media Criticisms on Tuition Fee Policies at State Universities in Indonesia
publicationTitle: 2024 11th International Conference on Electrical Engineering, Computer Science and Informatics (EECSI)
abstract: This study aims to identify public criticism on social media related to the residential tuition policy imposed in state universities in Indonesia. Knowing the public's criticism of the single tuition policy on social media can identify critical issues, understand the public sentiment, and provide insights for policy improvement. The benefits of the process can be used to improve the quality of policies, strengthen relations with the public, increase student satisfaction and welfare, and contribute to academic knowledge about policy analysis using social media. The data came from public comments about tuition fees on Twitter, You'Tube, Instagram, and TikTok platforms. The dataset was labeled as neutral, negative, and positive sentiment in the first step using IndoBERT's pre-trained model. The result of a negative sentiment of 62.26% from the dataset was then used for topic analysis using the Latent Dirichlet Allocation algorithm, and a different number of topics was obtained on each platform with topic compositions for Twitter, YouTube, Instagram, and TikTok of 10, 5, 2, 10 topics respectively. The results of the synthesis from all platforms concluded that seven themes are the main issues discussed in public criticism related to tuition fees, where the top three themes are criticism of government policies that increase tuition fees (48,60/0), corruption cases occur in state universities (20,3 %) and students' concerns about continuing their studies when there is an increase in tuition fees (12,5<sup xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">%</sup>).

articleTitle: Fliperentiation Learning using a Mix of Tat Twam Asi and HOTS-Superitem Logic Based on the Kelase Platform as a Renewable Learning Model
publicationTitle: 2024 11th International Conference on Electrical Engineering, Computer Science and Informatics (EECSI)
abstract: The decline in learning enthusiasm among students is caused by a monotonous learning process that does not accommodate students' learning needs adjusted to their differing abilities and interests. This problem must be overcome by presenting an innovation in the form of a Fliperentiation learning model design with a mixed Tat Twam Asi packaging and HOTS-Superitem logic based on the Kelase platform. This research aimed to show the initial design of the Fliperentiation Learning model with mixed Tat Twam Asi packaging and HOTS-Superitem logic based on the Kelase platform as a renewable learning model. This research used the Borg and Gall model development approach. The development stages in this 2024 research only focus on the research & field data collection stage, planning stage, design development stage, initial trial stage, and revision stage of initial trial results. The subjects involved in obtaining data from initial trials on the initial design of the Fliperentiation learning model were ten evaluators. The data collection tool for the initial trial results was in the form of a questionnaire. The data analysis technique from this research compares the results of initial trials of the Fliperentiation learning model design with effectiveness standards referring to the eleventh scale. The impact of the research results is that there is a positive response from educational evaluators and stakeholders in the health sector regarding the existence of a renewable learning model that can be applied to health universities to support the improvement of students' cognitive, affective and psychomotor abilities based on their desires and needs. The results of this research have shown the effectiveness of the Fliperentiation learning model design included in the great category. This is proven by the percentage of effectiveness of the model design of 86.40%.

articleTitle: An Improvement of Apple Leaf Diseases Detection Using Convolutional Neural Network Methods Based on Mobile Systems
publicationTitle: 2024 11th International Conference on Electrical Engineering, Computer Science and Informatics (EECSI)
abstract: One of the main problems in apple cultivation is leaf disease, which can reduce fruit production and quality. Some leaf diseases that commonly occur in apple plants are scab, cedar rust, black rot, and others. Various pathogens such as fungi, bacteria, and viruses can cause this disease and can spread through environmental factors and inappropriate cultivation practices. Treatment of foliar diseases in apple crops relies heavily on early diagnosis, effective pest and disease control, and the use of disease-resistant varieties. Therefore, early detection of apple leaf disease can help prevent other apple leaf diseases. This research uses a Convolutional neural network (CNN) algorithm with the Efficientnet-B7 architecture which is applied to a mobile system that uses Flutter technology to detect apple leaf diseases. With 8000 data, the results of this study are accurate in distinguishing or detecting apple leaf disease. After conducting several tests on various configurations, the most accurate results were loss 0.1007, accuracy 0.9642, validation-loss 0.0325, and accuracy value 0.9900. Apart from that, the f1 score for the accuracy, precision, recall, and confusion matrix stages is 0.99, or 99%.

articleTitle: Summarization of Scientific Articles using Hybrid SciBERT and Graph-Based Algorithms
publicationTitle: 2024 11th International Conference on Electrical Engineering, Computer Science and Informatics (EECSI)
abstract: In the ever-evolving information age, automatic text summarization is an important solution to address complex text processing problems, especially in scientific articles. Scientific articles often have complex structures and terminology, requiring methods to capture deep contextual meaning. This research proposes an extractive text summarization approach that combines SciBERT, a BERT-based language model developed specifically for scientific texts, with PageRank and HITS algorithms that are integrated using Harmonic Mean. SciBERT converts sentences in scientific articles into sentence vectors by combining the last four layers to produce optimal contextual embedding to preserve complex scientific meaning and context. Furthermore, PageRank and HITS algorithms rank sentences based on relevance and the relationship between sentences. Combining these two algorithms through the Harmonic Mean produces a more representative summary, balancing sentence relevance and overall text coherence. The approach was tested on the PubMed dataset, showing that the proposed model could produce summaries with ROUGE-1 scores reaching 32.23%, ROUGE-2 reaching 11.64%, and ROUGE-L reaching 29.18%. These results show that combining SciBERT with graph-based algorithms can effectively capture and retain important information in complex scientific texts while overcoming problems such as loss of context between sentences.

articleTitle: Multi-Networks of Motor Imagery and Asymmetric Channel Pair for EEG Stroke Scale Classification
publicationTitle: 2024 11th International Conference on Electrical Engineering, Computer Science and Informatics (EECSI)
abstract: Stroke disrupts the blood supply and nutrients to the brain, causing dysfunction or disability that reduces the patient's quality of life. Rehabilitation is required to restore function and independence. So, monitoring instruments such as an electroencephalogram (EEG) are required. EEG records the electrical brain activity, which needs feature extraction before classification. It is done to obtain variables that distinguish the stroke scale captured through EEG signals. Some of these are the ability to imagine movement or motor imagery and the difference in waves from symmetric channel pairs. This paper proposes a stroke scale classification method based on EEG signals using multi-networks of two-dimensional convolutional neural networks. Wavelet filters separate EEG signals into some frequency bands called waves. The multi-network capability allows CNN to map EEG signal variables into class features simultaneously. The 2D-CNN, with its precision in connecting inter-channel and inter-temporal signals, ensures reliable classification. The frequency bands of EEG signals represent the variables of motor imagery and the asymmetry of channel pairs. The experimental results show that motor imagery and asymmetric channel pairs based on EEG signals are characteristics of stroke levels. The proposed method, a multi-network 2D CNN, achieves an accuracy of 90.19%, 9% higher than that of a single network. In addition, multi-network 2D CNN also speeds up computation, which is very beneficial in EEG signals. The experiment also tested the fact that stroke information is almost identical in all channels. Motor imagery variables are slightly more accurate than the asymmetry of symmetric channel pairs.

articleTitle: Automatic Identification System Application Based on User-Centered Design and Human-Computer Interaction Design for Indonesian Fishermen
publicationTitle: 2024 11th International Conference on Electrical Engineering, Computer Science and Informatics (EECSI)
abstract: As the world's largest archipelagic country, Indonesia places a significant reliance on its fishing sector, which plays a pivotal role in the national economy and the well-being of local communities. Operational challenges frequently confront Indonesian fishermen, including concerns pertaining to safety, efficient navigation, and communication at sea. The Automatic Identification System (AIS) represents a potential solution to these challenges. Nevertheless, the implementation of AIS technology among traditional fishermen remains constrained by a dearth of technical comprehension and the challenges associated with utilising existing devices. Consequently, a mobile-based AIS application has been developed using and User-Centered Design (UCD) and Human-Computer Interaction (HCI) Design approaches, with the specific aim of addressing the needs of Indonesian fishermen. The chi-square test results also support these findings, showing a significant association between ease of navigation and satisfaction levels <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$(\chi^{2}=30.00,\ \mathrm{p}=0.00044)$</tex>. These results highlight the significance of an intuitive and user-friendly interface design in enhancing fishermen's satisfaction with the AIS application. It is, thus, recommended that the main focus of application development should be on improving ease of navigation and providing relevant and useful features. This study offers invaluable insight that will inform the further development and implementation of an effective AIS application for Indonesian fishermen.

articleTitle: Security and Privacy Relate Future Aspects of Artificial Intelligence-Powered Electric Vehicle Technology
publicationTitle: 2024 11th International Conference on Electrical Engineering, Computer Science and Informatics (EECSI)
abstract: Artificial Intelligence (AI) and electric vehicles EVs are revolutionizing the future of transportation, automation, and connectivity. The integration of AI in EV technology heralds a transformative era in transportation, characterized by enhanced efficiency, autonomy, and user experience. However, as AI-powered EVs become increasingly prevalent, critical security and privacy challenges emerge that necessitate comprehensive scrutiny. This paper explores the future aspects of security and privacy in AI-powered EVs, highlighting potential vulnerabilities and the implications of data exploitation. Key areas of focus include the cybersecurity threats posed by interconnected vehicle networks, the safeguarding of personal data from unauthorized access, and the development of robust encryption methods to protect vehicular communication systems. Additionally, the paper examines regulatory frameworks and industry standards essential for ensuring the secure deployment of AI in EVs. By addressing these concerns, the research aims to provide a holistic understanding of the measures required to fortify the security and privacy of AI-driven electric vehicles, ultimately contributing to developing a safe and trustworthy transportation ecosystem.

articleTitle: A Comparative Study of Machine Learning Algorithms for Predicting Project Outcomes
publicationTitle: 2024 11th International Conference on Electrical Engineering, Computer Science and Informatics (EECSI)
abstract: Crowdfunding platforms are online services that allow individuals and organizations raise capital for their various projects or initiatives. These platforms transform the way people can fund their ideas, products or activities. Among these platforms, Kickstarter is one of the most well-known and successful. It has facilitated the launch of thousands of projects, aiding creators bring their ideas to life with the support of generous backers, however, determining the outcomes of the project is a crucial decision-making for both creators and funders. Machine learning algorithms offer powerful tools for analyzing large amounts of data and identifying themes and patterns that can predict whether a project will be successful, fail, be canceled, remain live, or be suspended. By employing machine learning algorithms such as K-nearest Neighbors (K-NN), Decision Trees (DT), and Neural Networks (NN), three distinct models were developed to predict the status of Kickstarter projects. The results indicated that the Decision Tree algorithm outperformed both K-NN and NN in terms of accuracy, achieving a performance rate of 89.02%. This study highlights the significant potential of machine learning algorithms to predict outcomes that are essential for decision-making for creators and backers alike in crowdfunding-related activities.

articleTitle: An Initial Study in Historical Javanese Script Recognition Data Synthetic using Neural Style Transfer
publicationTitle: 2024 11th International Conference on Electrical Engineering, Computer Science and Informatics (EECSI)
abstract: Recognizing and digitizing Javanese scripts is challenging due to their unique characters and style, which traditional character recognition methods struggle to handle. This study uses neural style transfer with a pretrained VGG-19 model to create synthetic data, for improving character recognition accuracy. High-resolution scans of Javanese documents and printed fonts were used, split into training, validation, and test sets. Following this, a YOLOv9 object detection model was trained to identify and classify Javanese characters within the augmented datasets. The results indicate that the use of style transfer enhances detection performance, achieving a precision of 92.8%, recall of 91.5%, mAP50 of 92.4%, and mAP50-94 of 81.7%, outperforming previous methods. This demonstrates that the inclusion of style transfer and synthetic data generation increase the model's accuracy in recognizing complex historical texts.

articleTitle: Enhancing Accuracy in WBANs Through Optimal Sensor Positioning and Signal Processing: A Systematic Methodology
publicationTitle: 2024 11th International Conference on Electrical Engineering, Computer Science and Informatics (EECSI)
abstract: Wireless Body Area Networks (WBANs) have transformed fitness monitoring by providing continuous real-time data collection from small sensors placed on or inside the human body. Even though WBANs have important benefits, their accuracy and dependability are jeopardized by issues with sensor placement and signal processing. Incorrect sensor positioning can lead to inaccurate information, while noisy surroundings make signal processing more challenging. This focuses on using a single methodical approach to improve sensor placement and enhance signal processing in WBANs. We suggest a comprehensive solution that tackles placement sensitivity and noise reduction by combining anatomical modeling, real-time feedback mechanisms, and innovative machine learning algorithms. Experimental results show a 25% increase in signal quality and a 35% improvement in data precision when compared to conventional techniques. This method not only enhances the dependability of health monitoring systems but also validates their ability to be scaled and their effectiveness in various medical uses. Our results highlight the potential of WBANs to transform health care services, providing more accurate diagnostics and customized treatments.

articleTitle: The Evolution of Non-invasive Hemoglobin Measurement with IoT and AI-Based Optical Sensors
publicationTitle: 2024 11th International Conference on Electrical Engineering, Computer Science and Informatics (EECSI)
abstract: Hemoglobin measurement has significantly evolved with the integration of IoT and artificial intelligence (AI) technologies. This paper presents the evolution of non-invasive hemoglobin measurement using IoT and AI-based optical sensors. IoT and AI-based optical sensors have revolutionized the field of hemoglobin quantification, allowing us to measure this important biomarker in a way that isn't invasive or difficult to handle. The use of optical sensing technology, along with IoT frameworks and AI methods, has improved the accuracy and usefulness of hemoglobin tests, showing a promising way to improve healthcare outcomes. However, challenges remain in the field of non-invasive hemoglobin measurement, such as precision constraints, data security, and privacy safeguards. Despite these challenges, the future landscape of non-invasive hemoglobin measurement leveraging IoT and AI-powered optical sensors appears poised to transform healthcare delivery significantly. Together, IoT and AI-based optical sensors have the potential to revolutionize healthcare monitoring and diagnosis.

articleTitle: Handling Imbalanced Datasets in Researcher Scientific Classification Using Oversampling and Undersampling Approaches
publicationTitle: 2024 11th International Conference on Electrical Engineering, Computer Science and Informatics (EECSI)
abstract: The challenge of class imbalance in datasets is a prevalent issue in machine learning, often resulting in biased and inaccurate predictions. This study investigates the effectiveness of different data balancing techniques in enhancing classifier accuracy when applied to an imbalanced Indonesian National Scientific Manuscript dataset.
