Specifically, we examine how various classifiers respond to three widely used data balancing methods: Synthetic Minority Over-sampling Technique (SMOTE), Random Under-sampling, and Random Over-sampling. We assess the performance of six classifiers-Support Vector Machine (SVM), Logistic Regression (LR), K-Nearest Neighbors (KNN), Extreme Gradient Boosting (XGB), Naïve Bayes (NB), and Gradient Boosting (GB)-when these techniques are applied. The analysis reveals diverse outcomes, with some classifiers showing substantial accuracy gains, while others experience moderate or even adverse effects. The findings underscore the importance of selecting an appropriate balancing method based on the dataset's characteristics and the specific classification algorithm employed in the knowledge classification process.

articleTitle: Ksurf: Attention Kalman Filter and Principal Component Analysis for Prediction under Highly Variable Cloud Workloads
publicationTitle: 2024 11th International Conference on Electrical Engineering, Computer Science and Informatics (EECSI)
abstract: Resource estimation and workload forecasting are critical in cloud data centers. Complexity in the cloud provider environment due to varying numbers of virtual machines introduces high variability in workloads and resource usage, making estimations problematic using state-of-the-art models that fail to deal with nonlinear characteristics. High measurement noise and variance affect the estimation of resource metrics of cloud systems across packet networks influenced by external dynamics. An ideal solution to these problems is the Kalman filter, a variance-minimizing estimator, ideal for highly variable data with Gaussian state space noise such as internet workloads. This work provides a new solution by making these contributions: i) it introduces a novel Kalman filter estimator using principal component analysis and an attention mechanism, ii) it evaluates the scheme on a Google Cloud benchmark comparing it to the state-of-the-art Bi-directional Grid Long Short- Term Memory network model on prediction tasks and iii) demonstrates real-time performance through a control task using a cloud-based messaging system with predictive auto-scaling. The new scheme improves prediction accuracy by 37% over state-of-the-art Kalman filters in prediction tasks, reduces the time series prediction error of the neural network model by over 40%, and improves Apache Kafka workload-based scaling stability by 58%.

articleTitle: Oryza Sativa Disease Diagnosis Through Particle Swarm Optimized Shifted Windows Transformer
publicationTitle: 2024 11th International Conference on Electrical Engineering, Computer Science and Informatics (EECSI)
abstract: One of the primary problems farmers encounters is the frequent occurrence of diseases that specifically target the leaves of rice plants. This makes it extremely difficult for farmers to supply the rising demand for food needed to support an expanding population. The agricultural sector suffers substantial losses due to rice diseases, which greatly affect food production. Traditional methods of identifying diseases in rice leave have limitations in accuracy and computational efficiency. To tackle these challenges, this study introduces a novel approach: a rice leaf disease detection system employing the Shifted Windows Transformer (SWIN). This system represents a significant advancement in rice disease classification. Unlike conventional methods such as Convolutional Neural Networks (CNNs), which may struggle to capture the full context efficiently, Shifted Windows leverages hierarchical transformer blocks to better understand the complexities of images. By utilizing this architecture, the proposed system offers improved precision and computational efficiency in identifying rice leaf diseases from captured images from rice leaves giving high accuracy.

articleTitle: A Comprehensive Review of Image Segmentation Architectures
publicationTitle: 2024 11th International Conference on Electrical Engineering, Computer Science and Informatics (EECSI)
abstract: Semantic segmentation, the task of assigning class labels to each pixel in an image, is fundamental to numerous computer vision applications. This review paper critically analyzes six prominent segmentation architectures: Fully Convolutional Networks (FCN), U-Net, DeepLab, YOLO, SegNet, and Mask R-CNN, with evaluations primarily based on mean Intersection over Union (IoU) scores on the COCO dataset. FCN initiated the development of end - to-end trainable models for pixel-wise classification. U-Net's symmetric encoder-decoder architecture with skip connections has proven highly effective in biomedical image segmentation. DeepLab variants utilize atrous convolutions to enhance dense prediction tasks. YOLO, primarily recognized for real-time object detection, also supports segmentation with a balance of speed and accuracy. SegNet's straight-forward design and computational efficiency make it ideal for resource-constrained environments. Mask R-CNN extends Faster R-CNN by integrating instance seg-mentation with object detection. Performance evaluations reveal mean IoU scores as follows: FCN (0.35-0.55), U-Net (0.50-0.70), DeepLab (0.60-0.80), YOLO (0.55-0.65), SegNet (0.40-0.60), and Mask R-CNN (0.60-0.80). This review provides insights into the strengths, limitations, and application domains of these architectures, assisting researchers and practitioners in selecting appropriate models for specific segmentation tasks.

articleTitle: Implementation of Synthetic Minority Over-Sampling Technique in the Anaemia Classification Using the LSTM and Bi-LSTM Algorithms
publicationTitle: 2024 11th International Conference on Electrical Engineering, Computer Science and Informatics (EECSI)
abstract: Anaemiais a health disorder characterized by a lack of red blood cells in a person's body. Anaemia sufferers will tire more quickly, and their faces look paler than normal people's. Anaemia can occur over a short or long period (depending on the severity). If anaemia continues to be ignored, complications can worsen a person's health condition. Considering the impact caused by anaemia, a solution is needed to detect anaemia precisely and accurately. One way can be taken is by utilizing an artificial intelligence-based system to detect or classify anaemia based on its symptoms. Therefore, we tried to analyze factors related to anaemia in this study and carry out anaemia classification based on the LSTM and Bi-LSTM algorithms. The dataset used in this study came from the Kaggle repository, which contains medical record information for 1421 patients (620 patients diagnosed with anaemia and 801 patients with non-anaemia). The patient's medical record information includes gender, blood haemoglobin level, MCH, MCHC, MCV, and diagnosis results. In the research dataset, we also applied SMOTE to balance the data classes for anaemia and non-anaemia sufferers and compare the classification results' performance. Based on the research results, the haemoglobin level factor has the highest correlation value of 0.8 compared to other factors such as gender (0.25), MCHC (0.05), MCH (0.03), and MCV (0.02). Meanwhile, the classification results show that the use of SMOTE can increase the specificity (100%), precision (100%), F1-score (98.93%), and accuracy (98.86%) of the LSTM algorithm during the classification process.

articleTitle: Off-site and On-site Smart Feeding, Monitoring and Control System Designed for Commercial Tilapia Fishponds
publicationTitle: 2024 11th International Conference on Electrical Engineering, Computer Science and Informatics (EECSI)
abstract: This Aquaculture is a steady food source that replenishes aquatic species. To ensure the health of the fish in aquaculture operations, ensuring the quality of the water is paramount. Overfeeding and underfeeding have adverse effects directly on the fish and the water. Tilapia is a staple fish in the context of the Philippines and different fishes have different optimal growth parameters. Additionally, few studies are attempting to develop a complete fishpond automation system. Due to these, a complete system capable of automated feeding and water monitoring and adjustment for commercial Tilapia fishponds was developed. An on-site and off-site interface, a backup power supply, and several other features were also developed to enhance the prototype's functionality in a real-world environment, particularly in commercial fishponds. The ESP-NOW protocol provided close to real-time monitoring, demonstrating its usage in a fishpond setting. Each prototype's functionality was tested to ensure its accuracy and practical functionality for commercial Tilapia fishponds.

articleTitle: In-Depth Examination of Student Attrition in Higher Education Through Decision Tree, Random Forest, and XGBoost Algorithms
publicationTitle: 2024 11th International Conference on Electrical Engineering, Computer Science and Informatics (EECSI)
abstract: Customer Customer churn, a critical metric for businesses reliant on customer loyalty, involves the loss of customers from a company. This study examines churn among college and university students, leading to financial losses, decreased accreditation, and diminished reputations for educational institutions, ultimately reducing their appeal to prospective students. To identify factors contributing to student churn and classify students as likely to churn or not, this research utilizes Decision Tree, Random Forest, and XGBoost algorithms. These classification algorithms, with XGBoost and Random Forest enhancing Decision Trees through boosting and bagging techniques, respectively, are well-suited for the task. The data was sourced from the Academic Information Bureau and processed before model development. The model with the best performance will predict student churn on new, unseen data. Findings indicate varying performance metrics for each model, including accuracy, precision, recall, and F1-score. The XGBoost model excelled, achieving an accuracy of 98%, precision of 99%, recall of 96%, and an F1-score of 97%, significantly improving over the base Decision Tree model across all metrics. Notably, all models showed better performance in predicting the majority class (not churn) compared to the minority class (churn).

articleTitle: Decomposition-Based Backpropagation Neural Network Ensemble Processing Model for Exchange Rate Volatility
publicationTitle: 2024 11th International Conference on Electrical Engineering, Computer Science and Informatics (EECSI)
abstract: Exchange rate volatility forecast is critical for both the government and the private sector when making monetary policy. Thus, the goal of this research is to find an appropriate prediction model for exchange rate volatility. This study employs a decomposition-based Backpropagation Neural Network (BPNN) ensemble model. This model collects data through decomposition and then models it with BPNN to provide a single network prediction. Each IMF uses the same parameters: a 4-4-1 input-hidden-output neuron network architecture, sigmoid and identity activation functions, a learning rate of 0.1, and the Flecher-Reeves network training function. To avoid overfitting caused by repeated parameter selection attempts, the same parameters are employed. Furthermore, predictors are chosen using the Principal Component Analysis (PCA) and Correlation Based Feature Selection (CFS) approaches, and Ensemble BPNN is performed based on the predictor findings. The currency rate data utilized is from the last two years (2021–2023), with a big data spread (469.46), indicating strong volatility. The EMD decomposition approach includes 6 IMF and EEMD 7 IMF. This study demonstrates that the decomposition based on BPNN Ensemble can decrease errors for both decomposition techniques with a performance percentage of 92.78<sup xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">%</sup> and 98.72% for MSE and MAE compared to a single NN, the selection of a single network that is more capable of reducing errors is CFS, and the method developed is capable of tracking the movement of exchange rate volatility.

articleTitle: Sentiment Analysis of Quick Count Results of the 2024 Indonesian Presidential Election on Social Media
publicationTitle: 2024 11th International Conference on Electrical Engineering, Computer Science and Informatics (EECSI)
abstract: Sentiment analysis is a technique of analyzing text to determine the emotion of the message. The main objective of this sentiment analysis is to investigate whether Indonesian citizens on the platform X felt positive, negative, or neutral towards the Quick Count results of the recent 2024 Indonesian Presidential Election, in light of public distrust surrounding the legitimacy of the election organizers. The goal of this study is also to compare the performance of two classifier models; Naive Bayes and LSTM, based on standard metrics like accuracy, precision, recall, and f1-score. The data used were posts scraped from X taken after the election day on February 14th, along with datasets sourced from Kaggle and GitHub. The data preprocessing followed a sequence of data cleansing, case folding, and stop word removal. The final dataset is then split and vectorized using TF-IDF for Naive Bayes, and tokenized for LSTM. The result of this research shows 75.142% of accuracy for the Naive Bayes classifier and 80.03 % of accuracy for the LSTM-based classifier. From the 2,639 posts classified by the Naive Bayes model, 64.7% show positive sentiment towards the Quick Count results, whereas the LSTM model produced 58.2% positive sentiment of the same amount.

articleTitle: Hybrid Machine Learning Model for Anticipating Cyber Crime Malware in Android: Work on Progress
publicationTitle: 2024 11th International Conference on Electrical Engineering, Computer Science and Informatics (EECSI)
abstract: Improvements in information technology bring new challenges in cyber security, especially on the Android platform which is the main target of malware attacks. The National Cyber and Crypto Agency (BSSN) as the national cybersecurity institute recorded millions of attacks involving the Android Package Kit (.apk) application for electronic wedding invitations in Indonesia. This research aims to develop a hybrid machine learning model to detect and anticipate malware on Android devices, using algorithms such as Support Vector Machine (SVM), Random Forest (RF), and K-nearest neighbors (KNN). The main challenges are the limited number of representative datasets and the lack of effective detection techniquesThis research utilizes a primary server with a virtual machine (VM) to analyze the security of Android applications using mobSF and Frida, involving decompilation, TLS testing, and sensitive feature extraction. The system also depends on an Android emulator and Android Debug Bridge (ADB) for simulation, along with PostgreSQL, Job Scheduler, and Remote Desktop Protocol (RDP) for data management and task scheduling. The dataset comprises 1314 malware samples and 770 benign samples, totaling 2048 Android applications, with an average analysis time of 35 minutes per application. Through data collection and pre-processing, as well as model training and evaluation, it is hoped that the proposed framework can improve the accuracy of malware detection, making a significant contribution in protecting Android users from ever-evolving cyber threats. After performing a comparison using the algorithms mentioned above, it was found that the Random Forest algorithm showed the best performance with an accuracy of 97.11%, a precision of 97.22%, and a recall of 97.11%.

articleTitle: Emotion Recognition from Human Speech Using Linguistic and Paralinguistic Features Through a Soft Voting Approach
publicationTitle: 2024 11th International Conference on Electrical Engineering, Computer Science and Informatics (EECSI)
abstract: Emotions are intricate psychological and physiological reactions that arise in response to various triggers and influence how people interact with others, face challenges, and make decisions. When it comes to interpersonal communication, a person's emotions are typically conveyed through both verbal and nonverbal cues. Speech serves as an effective signal for recognizing emotions as it encompasses both linguistic and paralinguistic information. This study proposes an emotion recognition model that utilizes speech to identify emotions. The linguistic aspects of speech, which involve the contextual meaning of an utterance including the arrangement and choice of words, are considered. Additionally, the paralinguistic aspects, such as pitch and intensity, which influence a person's intonation and speech prosody, are included. The model comprises two subsystems, each separately trained. The probability weights from these subsystems are calculated and used with a soft voting ensemble classifier model to make final predictions based on five emotion classes. Through experiments, the soft voting ensemble approach in the emotion recognition model achieved an average accuracy performance of 81 %, which was significantly higher than the average accuracy performance of the individual approaches for each subsystem.

articleTitle: QR Code-based Digital Watermarking For Protecting Personal Information On CT-Scan Images
publicationTitle: 2024 11th International Conference on Electrical Engineering, Computer Science and Informatics (EECSI)
abstract: In the current digital era, the rapid exchange and transmission of medical images, particularly CT -Scan images, have heightened concerns about data security and privacy. This paper presents a robust digital watermarking method designed to protect sensitive patient information in CT -Scan images. The proposed approach integrates Discrete Wavelet Transform (DWT) and Singular Value Decomposition (SVD) with QR Code-based Visual Cryptography and hybrid RSA-AES encryption. The method begins by embedding the watermark in the high-frequency sub-bands of the image using DWT-SVD. The watermark, encrypted with AES and further secured by RSA encryption of the AES key, is converted into a QR code and scrambled using a Chaotic Logistic Map. This hybrid approach ensures data confidentiality, robustness, and resilience against various image processing attacks such as noise addition, cropping, scaling, and JPEG compression. Experimental results demonstrate high image quality, with an average PSNR of 37.9dB, and significant resistance to common attacks, validating the effectiveness of the proposed method in maintaining both security and image integrity.

articleTitle: Leveraging Transformer-Based Topic Modeling using BERTopic for Publication Venue Recommendation
publicationTitle: 2024 11th International Conference on Electrical Engineering, Computer Science and Informatics (EECSI)
abstract: Topic modeling has become essential in a variety of text mining applications, such as document clustering and recommendation systems. This study investigates the potential of BERTopic, a transformer-based method that leverages BERT embeddings to recommend publication venues. Traditional topic modeling methods are made better by BERTopic, which uses the deep contextual embeddings that BERT (Bidirectional Encoder Representations from Transformers) offers. This investigation assesses the efficacy of BERTopic in clustering academic papers according to their content in order to suggest appropriate publication venues. We also compare the performance between different kinds of pre-trained sentence embedding models and input types (title, abstract, and title+abstract). The experimental results indicate that BERTopic performs well with the GARUDA dataset, which comprises 5272 records from three different research subjects. The results emphasize the transformative influence of the transformer-based model. The best performance of all cases was 99.17% mean average precision in the Top 3 position, using Title+Abstract as input data and all-mpnet-base-v2 as the sentence embedding model.

articleTitle: Secure Automated Smart Home
publicationTitle: 2024 11th International Conference on Electrical Engineering, Computer Science and Informatics (EECSI)
abstract: This research paper delves into the realm of advanced home security systems, focusing on the implementation of cutting-edge technologies facilitating safe and secure living environment. The paper explores the integration of face recognition technology, sensor-based gas detectors, and smart door lock systems to fortify the homes against potential threats. By leveraging innovative solutions such as face encoding for identification, gas leakage detection for timely alerts, and real-time monitoring of door states, the Smart Home Security system offers a comprehensive approach to safeguarding residential properties. Through a structured methodology and the utilization of state-of-the-art sensors and communication protocols, the research paper aims to enhance the security infrastructure of modern homes, providing homeowners with peace of mind and a heightened sense of security.

articleTitle: Developing A Machine Learning-Based Computer Vision Model for External Defect Detection in Camera Components
publicationTitle: 2024 11th International Conference on Electrical Engineering, Computer Science and Informatics (EECSI)
abstract: In this article, through exploring the operational procedures of domestic component manufacturers, specifically the production process of cameras for technological products, it is evident that post-processing product defect control poses a significant challenge. This process requires intervention from experienced personnel to conduct manual inspections, which has led to decreased productivity and diminished reliability. Based on this scenario, this paper proposes a computer vision model to detect visual defects in camera components. Machine learning and deep learning will be the primary technologies applied to overcome this challenge. The proposed method is evaluated in terms of accuracy and high performance. However, the model still requires further architectural adjustments and increased training data to achieve optimal refinement. The gained results will significantly enhance the effective of industrial camera production.

articleTitle: Determining Positive-Negative Emotions in Male and Female Based on EEG Signals using Machine Learning Algorithms
publicationTitle: 2024 11th International Conference on Electrical Engineering, Computer Science and Informatics (EECSI)
abstract: Emotionsare vital in everyday human life as a controller of behavior, decision-making and as a means to determine product marketing strategy/ market research. All of these things are very dependent on human emotional conditions. In addition, in the development of the computational affective field, brain signal-based emotion recognition (EEG) has become a trending topic of current research. Therefore, we attempted to compare positive-negative emotions in men and women based on EEG using a Machine Learning algorithm in this study. A total of 20 male and 20 female participants recorded their EEG signals in the frontopolar and frontal areas of the brain. Then the EEG data is processed by filtering, removing artifact, and decomposing it into three sub-bands (alpha, beta, and gamma). The extracted signal features are Mean Absolute Deviation and Power Spectral Density. Based on the signal feature analysis results, it is known that the signal feature values (MAD and PSD) for women tend to be higher than for men. Meanwhile, several algorithms are used to classify positive and negative emotions, such as Naive Bayes, K-Nearest Neighbor, Support Vector Machine, and Random Forest. Based on the results of classification, the best accuracy rate was 95.8% (on positive emotions for male & female gender), 92.2% (on negative emotions for male & female gender), and 79.8% (on positive-negative emotions for male & female gender) using Random Forest algorithm.

articleTitle: Development of a Low-Cost Smart Embroidery Conversion Kit
publicationTitle: 2024 11th International Conference on Electrical Engineering, Computer Science and Informatics (EECSI)
abstract: The increasing demand for embroidered garments confronts MSEs in developing countries, which have limited access due to the high cost of embroidery machines and digitizing software. This paper describes developing a detachable embroidery conversion system utilizing Raspberry Pi and Arduino combo for the control system and a Python-based digitizing software. A CNC plotter-like X-Y table with an embroidery hoop and externally geared Z-axis attachment (32:12 ratio) was designed for embroidery conversion and a darning foot for multi-directional sewing. The embroidery system includes a web-based digitizing software with 3-step Python parsing that converts images to embroidery G-Code. The assessment of the developed embroidery system in terms of accuracy was done on closed squares with varying contour widths. Analysis of all 16 segments per design revealed an accuracy of 89.28%, revealing a negative correlation between contour width and accuracy. Wider contours showed decreased accuracy compared to narrower ones, highlighting the significant influence of contour width on the final embroidered shape. This embroidery system is a low-cost alternative to conventional machines and digitizing software subscription fees. The detachable embroidery system's low cost and expanded functionalities position it as a potential driver for adopting embroidery throughout the textile value chain in domestic fabric and apparel MSEs.

articleTitle: ASDenseFormer: A Video-Based Autistic Self-Stimulatory Gesture Recognition Using DenseNet121 and Transformer Model
publicationTitle: 2024 11th International Conference on Electrical Engineering, Computer Science and Informatics (EECSI)
abstract: Complex human actions in healthcare set-tings may now be understood thanks to developments in deep learning and contactless sensors. Several computer vision-based deep learning algorithms have been developed in particular to enable a comprehensive analysis of human gesture recognition, including repet-itive movements. The most typical repeated motions that children with autism exhibit include spinning, head banging, and arm flapping. We present ASDense-Former, a hybrid model developed in this work to recognize repeated autistic movements in real time. The Self-Stimulatory Behavior Dataset (SSBD), which is available to the public, is used in this model. The Transformer model's self-attention principle handles the temporal information and classifies them, while DenseNet121 extracts spatial properties from video frames. We demonstrate that using a DensNet121 in conjunction with the Transformer model yields the best outcomes by carefully examining feature extraction and learning methodologies. Our model performed 10% better than the state-of-the-art works with an average accuracy of 86.66% in identifying the three repeating movements.

articleTitle: Hidden Markov Model Approach to Predict Performance Improvement of 4G Cellular Network
publicationTitle: 2024 11th International Conference on Electrical Engineering, Computer Science and Informatics (EECSI)
abstract: The automation of performance optimization in 4G cellular networks remains a significant research challenge. Although advances in artificial intelligence, machine learning, and deep learning have been made, their application in cellular networks is still in its early stages. The evolution of automated learning algorithms in these networks requires continuous optimization to improve performance. This research aims to develop a data analysis model using a Machine Learning approach to predict 4G network Key Performance Indicators (KPIs) and enable automated assessments. The study employs Hidden Markov Models (HMM) to predict KPIs such as eRAB Drop Rate and Setup Success Rate. Data were collected from 1,600 newly deployed sites of a mobile operator in Indonesia over six months, from July 2023 to January 2024. The findings indicate that HMM models can significantly contribute to understanding and enhancing cellular network performance. For instance, the model achieved an accuracy of 99.52% and an F1 score of 99.76% in predicting the eRAB Drop Rate. The Inter-Frequency Handover Success Rate showed 96.15% accuracy and a 97.99<sup xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">%</sup>F1 score, while the RRC Connection Setup Success Rate achieved 91.35% accuracy and a 95.29% F1 score. These metrics highlight the model's effectiveness in predicting KPIs. By utilizing HMM models for high-accuracy KPI analysis, network operators can gain deeper insights into network performance and implement targeted improvements. This approach presents a promising avenue for automating and enhancing performance in 4G networks.

articleTitle: Enhancing Security in Digital Twin Ecosystems: A Lightweight Cryptographic Algorithm Perspective with TinyJambu
publicationTitle: 2024 11th International Conference on Electrical Engineering, Computer Science and Informatics (EECSI)
abstract: N the context of Internet of Things (IoT) ecosystems, ensuring the authenticity and security of device interactions is paramount. This study presents an authentication framework designed to validate the identity of physical IoT devices and their corresponding Digital Twins (DTs) within the Eclipse Ditto platform. Leveraging the lightweight yet robust tinyJAMBU authenticated encryption algorithm, our approach guarantees both data confidentiality and authenticity. To bolster the security afforded by tinyJAMBU, the authentication process demands a precise match between the decrypted cipher and the Digital Twin's unique ThingID. The system's integrity is enhanced through the dynamic creation of bidirectional communication channels exclusively post-authentication, ensuring that only authenticated devices can access and modify Digital Twin features. Additionally, all communication between the Digital Twin and the devices occurs over secure channels established using TLS/SSL over MQTT, mitigating risks such as Man-in-the-Middle attacks and eavesdropping. Our performance evaluation, which measured execution times, power consumption, and CPU usage. Power consumption for TinyJAMBU-128, TinyJAMBU-192, and TinyJAMBU-256 without TLS was 8 mAh, 8 mAh, and 9 mAh, respectively, and with TLS was 8 mAh, 9 mAh, and 10 mAh. CPU usage during encryption for TinyJAMBU-128, TinyJAMBU-192, and TinyJAMBU-256 was 46.20%, 49.20%, and 50.60% without TLS, and 46.80%, 49.45%, and 57.60% with TLS, respectively. Our comprehensive security analysis affirms the robustness and efficiency of the proposed scheme against prevalent threats.

articleTitle: Optimization of Economic Scheduling for Generators Using Snake Optimizer Algorithm
publicationTitle: 2024 11th International Conference on Electrical Engineering, Computer Science and Informatics (EECSI)
abstract: Currently, the cost of fuel in the electrical generation is the largest cost to produce electricity. The emission problem which raises environmental pollution needs to be considered because it can adversely affect the surrounding environment and cause global warming. The effect of valve settings commonly referred to as the Valve Point Effect (VPE) can cause amount of fuel consumption related to the cost. In addition, there are transmission losses (power losses) in the electricity delivery process to be considered. Solving the problems have been conducted using vary of metaheuristic algorithm. In this work, a novel metaheuristic algorithm as known as Snake Optimizer (SO) will be applied to optimize power plant scheduling with involving of several factors such as fuel, emission, valve point effect, and power losses. The snake optimizer algorithm is tested for reliability on IEEE 30 Bus electrical system test data using 6 generator units. The test are carried out with various power load percentages from 141.70 MW (50%) up to 354.25 MW (125%), performace test with various parameter such as iteration, population, and solution time with same load is 283.4 MW. In addition, the optimization results of the snake optimizer algorithm will also be compared with other algorithms using the same load is 250 MW. The results show that snake optimizer algorithm can provide a good optimization solution and had more efficient cost. The research contribution with involving of factors such as fuel, emission, valve point effect, and power losses also made the calculation of cost more optimal, accurate and realistic.

articleTitle: Reference-Based Human Height Estimation
publicationTitle: 2024 11th International Conference on Electrical Engineering, Computer Science and Informatics (EECSI)
abstract: Human height estimation is one of the research fields used in digital forensics to assist forensic experts in digital image identification. Most of the research was specific to controlled environments, causing hard estimates of many variants of images. In other cases, estimating human height without additional information about the object is sometimes difficult. Therefore, we propose a human height estimation model based on reference objects. The proposed method consists of two significant steps. First, we calculate the height of the person and reference object in pixels. Second, we formulate a linear regression model with the 141 dataset that we calculated before. Then, we evaluate the model with two scenarios, normal and abnormal. The average estimation error is 1.76% with 72 data tests when tested in a typical scenario. Then, we have some results from the abnormal scenarios, i.e., 3.92 % for the arbitrary model, 1.56 % when there is no distance data, and 2.9% when the images are without reference objects. Although our model is not the best in terms of accuracy of estimation results, the error is relatively low considering the method we use and the image variant that can be estimated using our model.

articleTitle: Real-Time Water Meter Reading Based on TinyML
publicationTitle: 2024 11th International Conference on Electrical Engineering, Computer Science and Informatics (EECSI)
abstract: This paper proposes a system that automatically reads the value of the water meter using a tiny machine learning model (tinyML) running directly on the ESP32-CAM kit. A convolutional neural network (CNN)-based tinyML model is recommended to recognize meter digits before estimating a value. The digit recognition machine learning (ML) models were trained using three datasets generated from this study, including a grayscale image set, a contrast-enhanced image set using the HE algorithm, and a binary image set using the threshold determined by the adaptive threshold (AT) algorithm to find the matching set of images. The experimental results show that the proposed classification model with the input gray image and contrast-enhanced image gives the best accuracy of 98.3%, and the estimated speed is approximately 3 times per second. This accuracy is approximate compared to the previous study; however, the image data processing solution in this study provides roughly 10 times faster estimation time. Furthermore, the study shows that gray images should be used directly for the digit classification problem instead of being contrast-enhanced or converted to binary Image.

articleTitle: Demand Forecasting on a Mobile-Based Inventory Application: A Case Study of Jaya Sentosa Store
publicationTitle: 2024 11th International Conference on Electrical Engineering, Computer Science and Informatics (EECSI)
abstract: Limited customization in existing inventory manage-ment systems hinders optimal stock management for businesses with unique needs. This study addresses this gap by developing a mobile-based inventory application specifically designed for Jaya Sentosa Store. The application utilizes demand forecasting to optimize restocking decisions. While various demand forecasting models exist (e.g., ARIMA, SARIMAX), selecting the most suitable model for a specific business can be challenging. Our research implements and compares the accuracy and runtime of several models (ARIMA, SARIMAX, Theta, Prophet, LSTM) to determine the optimal choice for Jaya Sentosa Store. We apply Scrum in the development process. Back-end and front-end development use JavaScript (JS) and Kotlin programming languages, respectively. We conduct several experiments to de-termine the most suitable forecasting model between ARIMA, SARIMAX, Theta model, Prophet, and LSTM. The test uses MAE (Mean Absolute Error), RMSE (Root Mean Squared Error), and runtime as parameters. When it comes to accuracy and consistency, the Theta model excels in the test. Besides its runtime score, Theta model has the best average MAE and RMSE scores. Theta model has an average runtime, MAE, and RMSE of 0.053, 3.951, and 3.226, respectively. We conduct black box testing on the inventory application with Jaya Sentosa Store where all the cases are valid.

articleTitle: Mental Health with Machine Learning: A Prediction-Based Intervention Chatbot for Mental Health Conversations
publicationTitle: 2024 11th International Conference on Electrical Engineering, Computer Science and Informatics (EECSI)
abstract: Academic mental health is crucial for university students as it directly influences their academic performance, personal well-being, and future professional development. Factors such as academic stress, social isolation, financial difficulties, and family expectations can negatively impact students' mental health. Early identification of these risk factors is essential for developing effective interventions to prevent more severe mental health issues. The development of a prediction-based intervention chatbot using a machine learning approach offers a promising solution. This research utilizes a dataset derived from the DASS-21 scale, which measures levels of depression, anxiety, and stress, comprising 424 records of question-and-answer variations to train the chatbot. The dataset was divided into training and testing sets with an 80:20 ratio, allowing for unbiased model evaluation. The study compared the performance of two machine learning models: Random Forest Classifier (RFC) and Multinomial Naive Bayes (MNB). Results showed that RFC outperformed MNB, achieving an accuracy of 82.5%, along with high precision, recall, and F1-score, demonstrating its effectiveness in identifying relevant conversations and providing appropriate interventions. Although MNB is faster and more efficient, its lower accuracy of approximately 66% presents a risk of inaccurate responses. These findings highlight the potential of using RFC in a mental health intervention chatbot to offer reliable and high-quality support, making a significant contribution to both mental health and computer science by providing an effective tool for detecting and treating mental health issues among university students.

articleTitle: Design and Development of a Transformer Condition Diagnosis System Application to Predict Purification Time and Life of a Transformer Based on Machine Learning
publicationTitle: 2024 11th International Conference on Electrical Engineering, Computer Science and Informatics (EECSI)
abstract: Transformers are equipment in high-voltage engineering that often experience abnormalities originating from internal or external sources. This abnormality causes disturbances, so it is necessary to diagnose faults in the transformer as early as possible so that fault predictions and maintenance actions can be carried out to maintain the quality of work on the transformer. An application was designed to diagnose the transformer's condition and predict purification time and transformer life to maintain the quality of the transformer's work. This application is designed to help make it easier to predict transformer conditions using dissolved gas analysis test results, oil scores, furan, and tap changer. The application design is done using the Python programming language and then converted into a mobile app using the React Native library framework with a simulator using Expo and connected to a database to store user data. The predicted data is for the GT 2.1 Excitation transformer, GT 2.1 Main Transformer, and GT 2.1 UAT transformer. Based on the application design, the test results were 100% successful; the system validated all the tests from the ten tests. The GT 2.1 Excitation transformer oil purification time is predicted to be 5697 days since the last test, and the transformer lifetime is predicted to be more than 15 years. The GT 2.1 Main Trafo transformer oil purification time is predicted to be 2697 days since the last test, and the transformer lifetime is predicted to be more than 15 years. The GT 2.1 Excitation transformer oil purification time is predicted to be 1866 days since the last test, and the transformer lifetime is predicted to be more than 15 years.

articleTitle: Classification of Crude Palm Oil Quality Using K- Nearest Neighbor (K-NN)
publicationTitle: 2024 11th International Conference on Electrical Engineering, Computer Science and Informatics (EECSI)
abstract: The value of agricultural exports in Indonesia is mostly contributed by crude palm oil (CPO). The productivity of the best quality crude palm oil is very important to consider to increase Indonesia's competitiveness in the global market. However, determining the quality of CPO is susceptible to subjectivity from one or more parties, so it requires an objective approach with a machine learning algorithm. This study applies K-Nearest Neighbor (K-NN) to classify CPO quality using data from 2019 to 2023, totaling 6,790 data. The parameters for determining CPO quality are based on the percentage of FF A, moisture, dirt, and DOBI contained in CPO. The study results showed that the K-NN model with a scheme of 90 training data and ten testing data using SMOTE, with a K value = 5, and the Manhattan distance calculation is the most optimal model with an average accuracy of 99.54%. Furthermore, the confusion matrix results showed an accuracy value of 99.68%, precision of 98.92%, recall of 100%, and F1-score of 99.45%. From these values, the K-NN method can classify CPO quality quite accurately.

articleTitle: Development of Rescue Drone integrated with Internet of Things Control for Beach Surveillance - Case Study at Glagah Beach
publicationTitle: 2024 11th International Conference on Electrical Engineering, Computer Science and Informatics (EECSI)
abstract: Indonesia's extensive coastline makes beach destinations a popular choice for both local and foreign tourists. However, beach tourism also has risks, such as high sea waves which can cause tourists on the beach to be swept away by the waves and drown. Another thing that causes accidents on beaches or at sea in Indonesia is the inadequate security system and technology for monitoring coastal areas and a lack of supervision, especially for coastal tourist attractions managed by villages or communities. Glagah Beach in Kulon Progo, Republic of Indonesia is one of the beaches that has many cases of tourists being swept away by the waves or drowning. Based on that background, this research aims to create and implement a rescue drone or rescue UAV (U nmanned Aerial Vehicle) which functions as a monitoring device for coastal areas. This study used in creating a rescue drone is Research and Development (R&D). This rescue drone is designed to assist beach tourism personnel and coastal residents in monitoring coastal and sea conditions, as well as rescuing people who are swept away by the waves. The rescue drone is equipped with a high-quality camera including an infrared camera for capturing videos and pictures at night. Additionally, the device can carry up to three buoys to aid in evacuating victims. The UAV drone control system is integrated with an Internet of Things (IoT) application, allowing for easy operation via an Android smartphone and providing the latest information about wave height and weather from BMKG (Meteorology Climatology and Geophysics Council).
